A planning session turns unplanned beads into fully specified ones and owns every UI decision with the navigator; one or more implementation sessions pick up a planned bead, implement it under TDD, get it reviewed by Copilot, merged, and loop.

The split only works if the plan is a real contract and if the agents cannot corrupt each other. A stress test against this repository found five ways the obvious design breaks or silently produces wrong results; the infrastructure children below are those fixes, and they must land before more than one implementation agent runs.

Full design, including the twenty decisions taken with the navigator, is in the children's plans and in the harness skills themselves.
acceptance_criteria:
One planner session and one implementer session carry a real bead from unplanned to merged, with no navigator action beyond the UI discussion during planning.
Two agents can run the smoke and PWA suites at once without testing each other's bundles.
Concurrent PRs no longer overwrite each other's bead state.
close_reason: All 11 children delivered; validated by a live trial on 2026-08-13 in which Cyclops took ah-5jm from claim to merge unattended under scripts/run-implementer

title: Stop agents colliding on a bead someone already claimed
description:
## Summary

Two agents keep starting work on the same bead. The cause is not carelessness — it is that a claim
looks abandoned within minutes of being taken.

`bd update <id> --claim` takes a **lease** with a short TTL, kept alive only by `bd heartbeat`.
Neither `CLAUDE.md` nor the `beads-workflow` skill mentions `bd heartbeat` at all, so no agent here
has ever sent one. A work cycle in this repo — RED, GREEN, REFACTOR, a full local gate, CI — runs an
hour or more against a TTL of roughly five minutes.

Observed, on a bead an agent had claimed ten minutes earlier and was demonstrably still working
(it had already wired a dependency from it):

```
◐ ah-xde · Remove the Classic map theme   [P2 · IN_PROGRESS]
Lease: expires in 1 min (heartbeat 3 mins ago)
```

`bd reclaim` is the reaper: it finds in_progress issues whose lease expired, **clears the assignee
and sets them back to open** so another worker can claim them. `bd update --force` documents itself
as being for "abandoned claims — crashed agent, expired lease". With nobody heartbeating, every live
claim in this repository matches that description exactly.

Three contributing findings:

- **The selection window.** The loop claims before branching, but exploration and planning happen
  first — one bead was planned for ten minutes before it was claimed. Selected-but-unclaimed work is
  invisible to every other agent.
- **Worktrees are not the problem.** All three worktrees resolve to the same Dolt database, so a
  claim is visible locally the moment it is written.
- **Cross-machine is.** Leases are node-local and write no Dolt commit; only status and assignee
  commit, and those travel only on `bd dolt push`/`bd dolt pull`. The skill says to push at session
  end, so a claim can stay invisible to another machine for an entire session.

`claim.ttl` is not a documented config key — `bd config get claim.ttl` reports "not set", and the
skill already records that `bd config set` accepts unknown keys silently — so lengthening the TTL is
not a reliable lever. The fix belongs in the instructions.

## Scope

Update `.claude/skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md` and `CLAUDE.md` (the symlink to
`.github/copilot-instructions.md`) with four rules, agreed with the navigator:

1. **Claim first.** `bd update <id> --claim` is the first action after choosing a bead — before
   exploring, planning or asking questions, not merely before branching. A failed claim means
   somebody else won; pick another bead.
2. **Heartbeat while working.** `bd heartbeat <id>` at every phase gate and before any long wait (a
   full smoke run, a CI watch). Heartbeats write no Dolt commit and no history, so the cadence is
   free.
3. **Never take over a claim unasked.** `in_progress` with an assignee is authoritative whatever the
   lease says. No `bd reclaim`, no `bd update --force`, no reassignment over a live claim without
   the navigator saying so — an expired lease here means "nobody heartbeated", not "the worker
   died".
4. **Push the claim immediately.** `bd dolt push` right after claiming, not only at session end, so
   another machine can see it. Keep the session-end push as well.

Record the lease behaviour itself in the skill's Traps section, so an agent that meets a stale lease
recognises it rather than reasoning from `--force`'s help text.

## Out of scope

- Changing `claim.ttl` or any beads configuration; the key is not part of the documented surface.
- A supervisor process running `bd reclaim` on a timer. That is the upstream design for dead-worker
  recovery, and it is exactly what must not run here while nothing heartbeats.

## Validation

- `bd heartbeat <id>` on a bead this session holds, confirming the lease moves forward — the one
  claim in the four rules that has never actually been exercised here.
- Re-read both documents end to end: the daily loop, the checklist and CLAUDE.md's work-package
  rules must agree with each other, since all three currently describe claiming.
- No code changes, so the gate is `pnpm run lint` for the markdown-adjacent tooling only.
acceptance_criteria:
The beads-workflow skill and CLAUDE.md both say to claim before exploring or planning, not merely before branching.
Both say to heartbeat during long work, naming bd heartbeat.
Both forbid bd reclaim, bd update --force and reassignment over a live claim without the navigator's approval.
Both say to bd dolt push straight after claiming, in addition to at session end.
The skill's Traps section explains the lease TTL and why an expired lease here does not mean an abandoned worker.

title: The diff view: read what changed between two turns
description:
## Summary

The surface of ah-jg6. Given a chosen pair of turns and the computed differences, show the player what changed: units added, removed and changed; region changes; and how the orders drafts differ.

## Scope

- The view itself, wherever the navigator puts it, showing all three kinds of change.
- Say plainly when nothing changed in a category, rather than showing an empty list.
- A change must be traceable back to the thing that changed — a unit named in the diff is a way back to that unit.

## Why this is its own bead

Its shape is a navigator decision and needs mockups, and it is the only piece of ah-jg6 that cannot start until the other three have landed.

## Out of scope

- Computing the differences (ah-jg6.2) and holding the pair (ah-jg6.3).
- Editing anything from the diff view. Reading only.
- Diffing more than two turns, or across games.

title: Hold a second turn alongside the working one, and pick the pair
description:
## Summary

The app holds exactly one parsed report in memory (`parsed` in `AppShell`). To compare two turns it has to hold two, and the player has to be able to say which two.

## Scope

- Load a second, chosen turn alongside the current one without disturbing the working turn — selection, orders drafts and the map must all still refer to the turn being played.
- A way to pick the pair from the turns ah-jg6.1 enumerates.
- Make clear at all times which turn is the working one and which is being compared against, so the second turn can never be mistaken for the current one.

## Why this is its own bead

The picker is a surface the player sees and the navigator decides, and holding a second report touches the shell's central state. Doing that in the same bead as the diff rendering would put two risky changes in one PR.

## Out of scope

- The diff computation (ah-jg6.2) and the diff view (ah-jg6.4).
- Editing orders in the compared turn. It is read-only.
- Holding more than two turns.

title: Compute the diff between two parsed turns
description:
## Summary

The reading half of ah-jg6's comparison: pure functions that take two parsed reports and say what changed. No UI, no storage, no adapters.

## Why this is its own bead

It depends on nothing — it is a function of two `ParsedReport` values, both of which the app can already produce — so it can be built in parallel with ah-jg6.1 and proved entirely against the committed fixtures. It also carries the hard part: deciding what "changed" means for a unit that moved, for a region seen in one turn and not the other, and for an order draft that was reflowed but not altered.

## Scope

- Units: added, removed, and changed between the pair, with the changed fields named rather than a bare "changed".
- Regions: what differs between the two turns' knowledge of a hex, and the distinction between "this region changed" and "this region was not seen in one of the turns", which are not the same thing and must not be reported as the same thing.
- Order drafts: how the two turns' drafts differ.
- Every comparison is a pure module under `packages/shared`, unit-tested against real fixtures — there are consecutive-turn reports for several factions in `tests/fixtures/reports/`.

## Out of scope

- Rendering anything. The view is a sibling.
- Enumerating or loading turns — ah-jg6.1 and ah-jg6.2.
- Diffing more than two turns, or across games.
- Any change to parsing or order validation.

title: Enumerate the imported turns of a game
description:
## Summary

The first piece of ah-jg6. Today a turn can be loaded only by a known number or as "latest"; nothing can ask a game which turns it actually holds. Add that enumeration and carry it across the boundary. No UI.

## Why this is its own bead

It is a pure widening of an existing path — persistence, the two adapters and the hand-written `CoreClient` mirror — with no design decision in it and nothing for the navigator to choose. Everything else in ah-jg6 needs it, and two of the siblings need the navigator and mockups. Splitting it lets the plumbing land while the surface is still being drawn.

## Scope

- `listImportedTurns` through `crates/core-persistence` over the existing `imported_turns` table, keyed by game and faction.
- Carry it through `crates/core-wasm` and `crates/core-tauri`, and mirror it in the shared `CoreClient` in `packages/core-client`.

## Out of scope

## Context

The first piece of the epic `ah-jg6`. A turn can be loaded today only by a known number
(`load_imported_turn`, `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs:948`) or as "latest"
(`load_latest_imported_turn`, `:972`). **Nothing can ask a game which turns it holds.** Every sibling
in `ah-jg6` needs that, and so does anything else that wants to reason about the stored history —
`shouldConfirmOlderTurnLoad` (`packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.ts:39`) today compares the
report on screen against the file being opened, not against what is actually stored, because it has no
way to find out.

The one existing enumeration is inside `export_game` (`lib.rs:~536`), which already selects exactly
the columns a summary needs and orders them — it is the shape to copy, not to call.

This bead has no blocker and no UI. It widens one path from SQLite to `CoreClient`, and stops.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**`crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs`** — the new type beside `ImportedTurnKey` (`:116-138`) and the
new function beside the two loads:

```rust
pub struct ImportedTurnSummary {
    pub key: ImportedTurnKey,
    pub season: Option<String>,
    pub imported_at: String,
    pub updated_at: String,
}
pub fn list_imported_turns(database_path: &Path, game_id: &str)
    -> Result<Vec<ImportedTurnSummary>, PersistenceError>;
```

Decisions taken here, and why:

- **Keyed by game only, like `load_latest_imported_turn` and `export_game`.** Every faction's turns
  come back, each row carrying its own `faction_id`, and the caller filters. A game with merged reports
  legitimately holds turns for more than one faction, and a signature that hid them would have to grow
  a second function later.
- **`ORDER BY turn_number ASC, faction_id ASC`.** A list of turns belongs in turn order, and the
  existing index `imported_turns_game_turn_idx (game_id, turn_number)` already covers it.
- **No migration.** Every column needed exists. See the traps — adding one anyway is actively harmful.
- **`season`, not month and year.** Month and year are *not* columns; they live only in
  `ReportHeaderInfo`, which comes from a full parse of `raw_report` and is not stored. What *is*
  reachable is `ReportParseResult.turn_header.season` inside `parsed_payload_json`. Read it with a
  small local `#[derive(Deserialize)]` peek struct rather than deserializing the whole payload — the
  peek has no dependency on `atlantis-core`'s types and survives that struct changing shape.
- **Guard as the other reads do:** `if !database_path.exists()` returns
  `PersistenceError::DatabaseFileMissing`. A missing database is an error; an empty table is an empty
  vector.

**`crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs`** — `list_imported_turns_state`, in **both** cfg arms, following
`load_imported_turn_state` at `:886-907` (native) and `:1072-1084` (the wasm32 stub returning
`"game persistence is not linked in this wasm32 build"`). A `ImportedTurnSummaryDto` beside the DTOs at
`:254-270`, reusing the existing `ImportedTurnKeyDto`.

**`crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs`** — `command_list_imported_turns`, following
`command_load_imported_turn` at `:723-739`, with a DTO beside `:152-157`. Note this crate reuses
`OrderDraftKeyDto` as its key type where core-wasm has its own; follow each crate's local precedent
rather than inventing a third key DTO.

**`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`** — three edits: the symbol in the `use atlantis_hud_core_tauri::{…}`
block at `:5-18`, a `#[tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case")]` wrapper, and the name in

**`packages/core-client/src/index.ts`** — six edits, all with an existing neighbour to copy:
`CoreAdapter` (`:828-834`), `CoreClient` (`:1046-1059`), `WasmBindings` (`:1076`), a
`ImportedTurnSummaryWireShape` accepting both casings (as `ImportedTurnRecordWireShape` at `:741`

`createCoreClient` (`:1725-1739`), `createWasmAdapter` (`:1937-1942`), `createTauriAdapter`

**`packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts`** — the third adapter, easily forgotten. It needs no

## Increments

1. **Listing.** *Test:* `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs`, in the inline `mod tests` at `:1471` —

2. **The boundaries of the query.** *Tests:* `a_game_with_no_imports_lists_no_turns` — an empty vector,

4. **Turns list in turn order regardless of faction.** *Test:*

5. **The Tauri surface.** *Test:* `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs` — `command_list_imported_turns_reports_every_committed_turn`,

7. **Boundary parity.** *Test:* `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts`, following the pattern at

   `createMemoryWebStore()` and `fakeWasm()` (`:12`) — "lists every imported turn of a game" and
   "lists no turns for a game that holds none", asserting the same shape the native path returns.

## The test plan

Rust, inline `mod tests`, `tempfile::tempdir`, `.expect("a sentence")` on every `Result`, `assert_eq!`
on whole structs or one projected field — the house style throughout `core-persistence`:

- `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs` — increments 1 to 4: ordering, per-game isolation, the empty
  game, the missing database, the season, and the unreadable payload.
- `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs` — increment 5.

TypeScript, vitest:

- `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts` — increment 7, the wasm/tauri parity and the literal invoke

  parity test exists at all.
- `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts` — increment 8.

Suites that must run: `cargo test --workspace`, `pnpm test`, then `pnpm check` before the PR.

No browser smoke test. Nothing visible changes, and the smoke suite drives the UI; the parity and
adapter tests are where this bead is actually proved.

## User-facing decisions

**None.** This bead adds no UI, changes no rendering, and alters nothing the player can see. The
surfaces that will consume it are the siblings `ah-jg6.3` (holding and picking a pair of turns) and
`ah-jg6.4` (the diff view), both of which need the navigator and mockups before they can be planned.

## Out of scope

- Any UI, picker, chooser or indicator. Siblings `ah-jg6.3` and `ah-jg6.4`.
- Loading a second turn into memory (`ah-jg6.3`) and computing any difference (`ah-jg6.2`).
- Changing what import writes, or adding a column to hold month and year. `season` is what is reachable
  without re-parsing, and it is enough to label a turn.
- Rewriting `shouldConfirmOlderTurnLoad` to check against storage. It becomes possible with this bead
  and is a genuine improvement, but it is a behaviour change to an existing confirmation and belongs in
  a bead of its own.
- Paging or filtering the list. A game holds tens of turns.
- Any change to `load_imported_turn` or `load_latest_imported_turn`.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test --workspace
pnpm test
pnpm check
```

By hand: with a game that has several turns imported (the fixtures under `tests/fixtures/reports/`
include `neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t70`, `-t71`, `-t72` and `-t74` for one faction, which is exactly the
case to use), call the new client method from a scratch test or the browser console and confirm it
returns four rows in turn order with the right seasons. Nothing in the app changes, so there is nothing
to click — the absence of any visible change is itself part of what to check.

## Known traps

- **Do not add a migration, and do not bump `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`.** Every column this needs already
  exists, and the index `(game_id, turn_number)` already covers the query. `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`
  (`lib.rs:12`), the `MIGRATIONS` array (`:35`) and the test
  `schema_version_tracks_the_latest_migration` (`:1962`) must agree; bumping one for a change that
  needs no SQL breaks that test and adds a migration that does nothing for ever after.
- **The new wasm binding needs both cfg arms.** `core-wasm` compiles twice, and **persistence is not
  linked into the wasm32 build**. Copy both halves of `load_imported_turn_state` — the native one at
  `:886-907` and the stub at `:1072-1084`. A binding with only the native arm does not fail politely.
- **`#[tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case")]` means JS passes `database_path`, not
  `databasePath`.** A camelCase key does not error — it arrives as a *missing argument*. This has bitten
  the repository before, which is why `index.test.ts:754` and `:830` assert the literal invoke argument
  names; the new parity test must do the same.
- **serde does not propagate `rename_all` into nested structs.** Every new DTO carries its own
  `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`, or a field crosses the boundary as `imported_at` while the
  hand-written mirror says `importedAt` — and TypeScript cannot catch it, because the mirror is
  hand-written. It simply reads `undefined`.
- **`serde_wasm_bindgen` can emit `undefined` where you expect `null`.** `createCoreClient`'s
  `loadLatestImportedTurn` body already handles both for that reason. An empty list may arrive as
  `undefined` rather than `[]` — normalize it to `[]`, and let the caller never see the difference.
- **There are three adapters, not two.** `createWasmAdapter`, `createTauriAdapter`, and
  `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts`, which is what the web build actually uses. Missing the
  third leaves the method throwing only in the browser, where no unit test looks unless you add one.
- **Adding a method to `CoreClient` does not break the test doubles.** They are local objects cast
  `as unknown as CoreClient` (`packages/shared/src/gameMemory.test.ts:61`,
  `orderDraft.test.ts:49`), so a double that lacks the new method fails at *runtime* with "not a
  function", not at typecheck. Expect that failure rather than reading it as a mistake.
- **`parsed_payload_json` holds `ReportParseResult`, the flat summary — not the full model, and not
  `ReportHeaderInfo`.** `month` and `year` are not in there; `turn_header.season` is. Do not plan on
  reaching a month.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — another agent usually holds it in a worktree. `git fetch origin main`
  and branch from `origin/main`.
- **Ignore `.claude/worktrees/`** when grepping; those are other agents' in-flight duplicate checkouts.

title: Toggleable region decorations on the map
description:
Atlantis hexes are grouped into named regions (called "province" in this codebase — `HexNode.province` / `StoredRegion.province` in packages/shared/src/hexMapModel.ts, `ReportRegion.province` in crates/core/src/report/model.rs). Right now a province is only ever shown as a per-hex label; there is no grouping structure that collects the hex ids belonging to one province, and no visual on the map that shows where a province's boundary actually is.

This bead adds a toggle that decorates the map with regions: for every known province, outline the superset of all hexes currently known to belong to it, and display the province's name centered in that outlined area.

The map (packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx) is SVG-rendered, and already has two toggle mechanisms this should plug into rather than inventing a third — packages/shared/src/workspace/LayerChips.tsx's LayerName/layers toggle, and the badge system (BadgeMenu, BadgeName/badges) in workspaceStore.ts. packages/shared/src/workspace/routeOverlay.ts is an existing SVG overlay-on-top-of-the-hex-grid this can follow as a pattern for drawing the outline.
design:
## Context

Every hex carries a province name (`HexNode.province`, `packages/shared/src/hexMapModel.ts:23`), but
nothing on the map shows where a province *is* — the name appears only in a hex's accessible label
and in the region panel. There is no grouping of hexes by province anywhere in the repository, and no
union-of-hexes outline of any kind; the nearest precedents are the route overlay and the marquee,
both of which draw per-hex polygons rather than a merged boundary.

When this lands, the map can be decorated with the provinces the faction has discovered: each
connected group of same-province hexes is outlined, and the province's name is written across it in
the manner of a printed atlas. The switch is a `Regions` entry in the existing Badges menu.

This bead has no blocker — nothing is waiting on unlanded work, and every file named below exists on
main today.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**New — `packages/shared/src/workspace/regionDecorations.ts`.** A pure module, no React, following
`packages/shared/src/workspace/routeOverlay.ts` as the precedent for "overlay as a pure function,
MapCanvas renders it". Unlike `routeOverlay` it must also produce geometry, because the boundary has
no existing helper to lean on. Suggested surface:

```ts
export type RegionPiece = {
  province: string;
  hexCount: number;
  outline: string;   // one SVG path `d`, world units, unordered M/L segment pairs
  label: { x: number; y: number; text: string; fontSize: number; letterSpacing: number };
};
export function regionDecorations(hexes: HexNode[], level: number): RegionPiece[];
```

**Reuse rather than reinvent:**

- `COLUMN_PITCH`, `ROW_PITCH`, `worldOf` — `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewport.ts:23-27,96`.
  These are the pitches MapCanvas actually renders with. `hexMapModel.ts` carries a *second*, parallel
  implementation of the same flat-top maths (`hexToPixel`, `hexCorners`); do not use it here.
- The corner maths in `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapHexView.ts:134-141` — flat-top, vertex due
  east, `angle = 60·k` degrees. If the `corner` helper is not exported, export it; do not write a
  third copy of this maths.
- `regionIdOf(coordinate)` — `hexMapModel.ts:94` — for keying the hex index (`z:x,y`).
- `allBadges` / `badgesFromStorage` — `mapThemes/hexView.ts:155`, `workspaceStore.ts:140`. Persistence
  and the default come free from these; nothing new is needed in the store.

**Edited:**

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/hexView.ts` — add `"regions"` to the `BadgeName` union
  (:123) **and** an entry `{ name: "regions", label: "Regions" }` to `BADGES` (:135). `BadgeMenu.tsx`
  is fully data-driven off `BADGES` and needs no edit at all.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx` — one new `<g data-testid="region-decorations">`
  inside `<g ref={worldRef}>`, inserted **immediately after `<theme.RoadLayer>` (:768) and before the
  route overlay group (:770)**, so routes, marks, the selection ring and the hit layer all paint above
  it. Rendered only when `badges.regions`. The pieces are computed in a `useMemo` keyed on the
  level-filtered hex array and `badges.regions`, alongside the existing memos at :215-232.
- `packages/shared/src/theme.css` — `.region-outline` and `.region-name`, next to `.map-label`
  (:165-177), plus a `.map-far .region-name { display: none }` LOD rule.

**Tests:** new `regionDecorations.test.ts`; edits to `MapCanvas.test.tsx`, `BadgeMenu.test.tsx`,
`workspaceStore.test.ts`, and `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`.

**Note the decorations are not a theme mark.** `LayerProps` is `{ views: HexView[] }` and a theme may
not read the settings store (`mapThemes/mapTheme.ts:20`); badges are consumed once, per hex, inside
`buildHexView`. A region decoration spans many hexes, so it belongs to MapCanvas, which already
receives the whole `badges` record as a prop (:119,164). No theme file is touched.

## Increments

Each opens with a failing test.

1. **Grouping into connected pieces.** *Test:* `regionDecorations.test.ts` — "groups the hexes of one
   province into a single piece, and a province discovered in two places into two pieces". Flood-fill
   over the six neighbour offsets `[1,1] [0,2] [-1,1] [-1,-1] [0,-2] [1,-1]`, joining only
   same-province neighbours. Hexes whose `province` is empty are skipped entirely, never grouped into
   a piece named `""`.
2. **The boundary path.** *Test:* "a lone hex outlines as six edges" (six `M` commands) and "two
   adjacent hexes of one province share no interior edge" (ten, not twelve), plus "the shared edge's
   midpoint appears in no segment" — that last one is what pins edge index `k` to the right neighbour
   offset. For each hex, for each edge `k` (corner `k` → corner `k+1`), emit the segment only when the
   neighbour across it is not in the same piece.
3. **Label placement.** *Test:* "the label sits at the centroid of a compact piece", and — the one
   that matters — **"for an L-shaped piece whose centroid falls outside it, the label anchors to the
   centre of the piece's hex nearest that centroid"**. The navigator's rule is that a name never
   floats over ground the province does not own, so the raw centroid must be snapped onto an owned
   hex whenever it lands off the piece.
4. **Fitting the label to the piece.** *Test:* "a name that fits keeps full size"; "a long name on a
   three-hex piece scales down"; "the scale never falls below the floor, and the name is still
   emitted". An atlas sets a name to the size of the thing it names:
   `span = (maxX − minX + 2R) · 0.94`, `natural = text.length · (0.62·fontSize + letterSpacing)`,
   `k = clamp(span / natural, 0.42, 1)` applied to font size, letter spacing and halo width. Base
   values `fontSize 11`, `letterSpacing 3.4` in world units, as drawn in the mockup. Below the floor
   the name overflows its outline rather than disappearing — that is the decision, not a bug.
5. **The badge.** *Tests:* `BadgeMenu.test.tsx` — "the menu lists Regions"; `workspaceStore.test.ts` —
   "regions defaults on, and a stored badge set saved before it existed still yields regions on"
   (`badgesFromStorage({ settlements: false })`). Then add the union member and the `BADGES` entry.
6. **Rendering.** *Tests:* `MapCanvas.test.tsx` — "draws an outline and a name for every piece when
   the regions badge is on"; "draws nothing when it is off"; "the decorations sit after the roads
   layer and before the marks layer", asserted in the same style as the existing layer-order test.
7. **Growing as more is discovered.** *Test:* `regionDecorations.test.ts` — "a piece that gains an
   adjacent hex outlines the larger area, and two pieces that grow together become one". The
   component test cannot prove reactivity (zustand serves initial state to
   `renderToStaticMarkup` — see the note at `LayerChips.test.tsx:31-35`), so the live behaviour is
   proven in the smoke suite instead.
8. **Smoke.** *Test:* `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` — "region decorations can be turned off from the
   Badges menu, and the choice survives a reload", modelled on the existing badge test at :981.

## The test plan

Unit (vitest, `renderToStaticMarkup` from `react-dom/server` — there is no testing-library in this
repo, and component assertions are regex/`toContain` over the markup string):

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/regionDecorations.test.ts` — grouping, disjoint pieces, the six-edge
  and ten-edge perimeter counts, the shared-edge-absent assertion, centroid, centroid-snapping for a
  concave piece, the fit scale at full size / reduced / floored, empty-province hexes skipped, and
  hexes on another level excluded.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.test.tsx` — presence and absence by badge, and the layer
  ordering (roads → decorations → route → marks).
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/BadgeMenu.test.tsx` — the `Regions` row exists.
- `packages/shared/src/workspaceStore.test.ts` — default on, and reconciliation of a pre-existing
  stored badge set.

Browser: `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`, the toggle and its persistence across a reload.

Suites that must run: `pnpm test` (packages, tooling, cargo) and `pnpm check` (adds lint, typecheck,
smoke, web build, pwa, fmt, clippy).

## User-facing decisions

Mockup: **`docs/ui/region-decorations.html`** (merged as PR #169). Three treatments, three rules for a
province found in two pieces, and three homes for the switch were drawn and put to the navigator.

- **Treatment: C, the atlas label.** A soft dashed boundary, and the name set widely letterspaced
  across the piece. Rejected: A, a thin brass ink boundary with a small centred label; B, the same
  plus a faint per-province colour wash — a second colour system on top of terrain and staleness.
- **A province known in two pieces: name every piece.** Each connected blob is outlined *and* named,
  so a province found twice is written twice. Rejected: naming only the largest piece, and naming only
  pieces of three hexes or more.
- **The switch: an entry in the Badges menu, labelled `Regions`.** Rejected: a fourth layer chip beside
  Staleness and Movement, in either default state.
- **Default: on**, like every other badge — `badgesFromStorage` reconciles against `allBadges(true)`,
  so existing players see region names appear after the update and can switch them off.
- **Wording: `Regions`**, not `Provinces` and not `Region names`, even though the code and the report
  call the field `province`.
- **The label is fitted to the piece it names**, down to a floor of about 42% of full size; a piece too
  small to hold its name at that floor keeps the name and lets it spill past the outline, as a paper
  atlas does with a small island.

## Out of scope

- Clicking or hovering an outline to select the province, or any interaction with the decorations.
- Per-province colouring or fills of any kind — treatment B was considered and rejected.
- Showing province membership or extent in the region panel or anywhere off the map.
- Drawing provinces from levels other than the one displayed, and any cross-level relationship.
- A legend, a province list, or a way to name or edit a province.
- Reconciling the two parallel hex-geometry implementations in `mapViewport.ts` and `hexMapModel.ts` —
  a real duplication, but not this bead's job.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm test
pnpm check
```

By hand, and only a human can do this: run the app, load at least two turn reports for one faction so
that a province is known partly from this turn and partly from memory, and confirm the decorations
match `docs/ui/region-decorations.html` — dashed boundary, letterspaced name, a name on every
connected piece. Then **cycle all five map themes** and confirm the outline and the label stay legible
against each palette, and zoom in and out and confirm the label neither swamps the map nor becomes
illegible before the far-zoom LOD hides it.

## Known traps

- **`allBadges` casts its result**, so adding `"regions"` to `BadgeName` *without* adding it to
  `BADGES` compiles cleanly and silently yields a record with no `regions` key — the menu row never
  appears and `badges.regions` is `undefined`. Add to both, in the same commit.
- **The label deliberately does not divide by `--map-scale`.** Every other piece of map text does
  (`.map-label { font-size: calc(9px / var(--map-scale, 1)) }`, `theme.css:165-177`) to hold a constant
  screen size. A label fitted to its piece's width must scale *with* the world, or it overflows the
  outline as you zoom out. Size it in world units and hide it at far zoom with the existing `.map-far`
  band class on the SVG root. Do not "correct" this to match `.map-label`.
- **Use the `font-size` longhand, never the `font` shorthand**, in the new CSS — every theme stylesheet
  carries this warning already, because the shorthand resets the `calc()` sizing.
- **MapCanvas's performance contract** (its doc comment at :135-154): pan writes no React state and
  `transform` is deliberately absent from the JSX. Compute the pieces in a `useMemo`; do not introduce
  anything that re-renders on pan or zoom.
- **Only coordinates where `x + y` is even exist.** Neighbours are `(±1, ±1)` and `(0, ±2)`. A naive
  `(±1, 0) / (0, ±1)` neighbour set finds no neighbours at all and silently produces one piece per hex
  — every hex outlined separately, which looks like a styling problem rather than a maths one.
- **`model.hexes` holds every level.** Filter on `coordinate.z === level` exactly as MapCanvas already
  does at :215-218, or an underground province merges with the surface one above it.
- **Hexes known only by name count.** A hex learned from another region's `Exits` block has a province
  and `knowledge: "named"`; the acceptance criteria say the outline covers everything currently known,
  not everything reported this turn. Do not filter on `knowledge`.
- **WebKit's driver returns `""` for text it considers clipped**, so a smoke assertion on the label's
  text content can pass on Chromium and fail in the native shell. Assert on a `data-testid` or an
  attribute, not on the rendered string.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled**, so a PWA run started
  straight afterwards fails with timeouts that look like a broken worker. Run `pnpm check`, which
  orders them correctly, rather than the suites by hand.
- **Ignore `.claude/worktrees/`** when grepping — it holds full duplicate checkouts of the repository,
  and a match there is another agent's in-flight branch, not main.

title: A faction view: attitudes, allowances and unclaimed silver
description:
## Summary

The showing half of ah-vp3. Once ah-vp3.1 has the data across the boundary, give the player
somewhere to read it: faction name, id and types; unclaimed silver; the status counts as
used-of-maximum; and the declared attitudes grouped by level with the default stated.

## Why this is its own bead

The shape of this surface is a navigator decision and needs mockups. All five collapsible panels are
hex- or unit-scoped, and every faction-scoped surface today is a header chip with a popover under it
(`MergedFactionsPanel`, `TurnMessagesPanel`). The header already renders `Faction <name>` with the
merged-factions chip hanging off it (`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx`), so an anchored
panel there — dismissed on Escape and on an outside press — probably fits better than a sixth dock
panel: this is read occasionally, not watched while planning. That is a proposal, not a decision.

## Scope

- The view itself, wherever the navigator puts it.
- Where a faction in the attitude lists is one whose report has been merged in, say so. Do not invent
  links to factions the app knows nothing about.
- Degrade rather than break on a report that carried neither block.

## Out of scope

- Writing or editing DECLARE orders — reading only, for now.
- How attitudes and allowances changed since last turn; that belongs with ah-jg6.
- Any faction-level statistic the report does not state.

## Depends on

ah-vp3.1, which puts the data on `ReportHeaderInfo`.
design:
## Context

The showing half of the epic `ah-vp3`. Its sibling **`ah-vp3.1`** is the reading half, and this bead
is blocked on it: `ah-vp3.1` puts `factionStatus` and `attitudes` onto `ReportHeaderInfo`
(`packages/core-client/src/index.ts:391`) and stops at the boundary, showing nothing. Read
`bd show ah-vp3.1` before starting — its plan names the field shapes, and its "Known traps" section
explains the serde naming hazard that decides what these fields are actually called at runtime.

The data this view will read, per `ah-vp3.1`'s plan:

```ts
header.factionStatus  // { entries: { label: string; used: number; maximum: number }[]; unparsed: string[] }
header.attitudes      // { defaultAttitude: string | null; levels: { attitude: string; factions: { name: string; id: string }[] }[] }
```

**If what landed differs, follow what landed** — the hand-written mirror in `core-client` is the
authority, not this plan. Do not begin until `ah-vp3.1` is merged; the field names cannot be guessed.

Alongside them, two fields have been parsed for months and rendered nowhere:
`header.unclaimedSilver` and `header.factionTypes`. Their only TypeScript references today are test
fixtures. This bead is their first consumer.

When it lands, the faction name in the header becomes a trigger, and behind it sits everything the
report says about the faction as a whole.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**New — `packages/shared/src/workspace/FactionPanel.tsx`.** Copy the shape of
`packages/shared/src/workspace/MergedFactionsPanel.tsx` (98 lines) almost line for line; it is the
closest existing surface and the one the navigator's choice points at:

- `absolute left-0 top-full z-20 mt-1 rounded border border-edge bg-panel-raised text-[11.5px]
  whitespace-normal shadow-lg` (`MergedFactionsPanel.tsx:63`) — `whitespace-normal` is required, the
  header sets `whitespace-nowrap`. Widen to about `w-80`; the mockup's popover is 284px.
- `role="dialog" aria-label="Faction"`, a `✕` close button with an `aria-label`.
- `onDragOver={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}` (`:60`) — **mandatory**; the header is the report-file
  drop target (`AppHeader.tsx:149`) and a floating panel that omits this becomes a drop zone.
- The dismissal effect at `:27-49`: `document` `keydown` for Escape plus `pointerdown` with a
  `panelRef.current?.parentElement` containment test, so pressing the trigger does not toggle twice.
- Body scroll region: `max-h-[40vh] overflow-y-auto`.

**New — `packages/shared/src/workspace/factionView.ts`.** Pure, no React, so the arithmetic is
testable without markup strings:

```ts
export type AllowanceRow = { label: string; used: number; maximum: number; fraction: number; atCeiling: boolean };
export function allowanceRows(status: FactionStatus): AllowanceRow[];

export type AttitudeLine = { attitude: string; factions: { name: string; id: string; merged: boolean }[] };
export function attitudeLines(attitudes: DeclaredAttitudes, mergedFactionIds: ReadonlySet<string>): AttitudeLine[];
```

`fraction` is `maximum > 0 ? used / maximum : 0`, and `atCeiling` is `maximum > 0 && used >= maximum`
— the real report's `Regions: 0 (0)` is neither full nor meaningful as a bar, and that distinction is
the whole reason this is a function rather than JSX.

**Edited — `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx:218-240`.** The faction name is plain text
today. It becomes a trigger in the shape every other chip uses (`type="button"`,
`aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded={factionOpen}`, a `▾` caret span with `aria-hidden`),
`data-testid="faction-chip"`. The header owns the button and the shell owns the panel and its state —
that is the split every popover here follows except Export, and there is a comment at `:137-143`
saying why Export is the exception. Three new props on `AppHeaderProps`: `factionOpen: boolean`,
`onFactionToggle: () => void`, `factionPanel: ReactNode`.

**Edited — `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`.** A `factionOpen` `useState` beside
`mergedOpen` (`:338`) and `messagesOpen` (`:331`), and the `<FactionPanel …>` node passed down.
`parsed` is plain React state at `:256` and the header is read inline (`factionLabelOf` at `:178`);
follow that, and do **not** add a store field. The merged faction ids come from the same `merged`
array already passed to `MergedFactionsPanel` — its records carry `mergedFactionId` (the testid at
`MergedFactionsPanel.tsx` is `merged-faction-${mergedFactionId}`).

**Reuse:** the token names in `packages/shared/src/theme.css:36-58` — `panel-raised`, `edge`,
`edge-soft`, `ink`, `ink-soft`, `ink-dim`, `brass`, `brass-bright`, `ok`, `danger`. Row separators
`border-t border-edge-soft py-1 first:border-t-0`; footnote prose `border-t border-edge px-2 py-1.5
text-ink-dim`.

**Deliberately not reused:** `useEscapeToDismiss` (`packages/shared/src/workspace/dismissLayer.ts:12`)
handles Escape only, via the layered dismiss stack, and none of the five header popovers use it — they
each hand-roll Escape *and* outside-press. Match the header popovers, not the dialogs; a faction panel
that dismissed on a different rule from the chip beside it would be the odd one out. Extracting the
five-way duplication into a shared `usePopoverDismiss` is tempting and is **out of scope** — see below.

## Increments

1. **Allowance arithmetic.** *Test:* `factionView.test.ts` — "reports used, maximum and the fraction
   for each entry, in the order the report printed them"; "a full allowance is at its ceiling"
   (`Mages 6 (6)`); "an allowance of zero out of zero is not at its ceiling and has no fraction"
   (`Regions 0 (0)`, the real degenerate case); "a status with no entries yields no rows".
2. **Attitude lines.** *Test:* "one line per level, in the order the report printed them";
   "a level the report printed as `none.` is kept, with no factions" — declared-and-empty, never
   omitted; "a faction whose report has been merged in is marked, and one that has not is not";
   "matching is by faction id, not by name".
3. **The panel renders.** *Test:* `FactionPanel.test.tsx` (vitest + `renderToStaticMarkup` from
   `react-dom/server`, string assertions, `resetWorkspaceStore()` in `beforeEach` — follow
   `RegionPanel.test.tsx:1-6`; there is no Testing Library in this repo) — "shows the faction name,
   id and types"; "shows the unclaimed silver"; "shows each allowance as used of maximum"; "shows
   each attitude level with its factions"; "states the default attitude".
4. **Degrading.** *Test:* "a report with neither block still renders the name and the silver";
   "a report with no unclaimed silver omits that row rather than showing null"; "an empty allowance
   list omits the whole Allowances section, heading included"; "an empty attitude list omits the whole
   attitudes section". This is the acceptance criterion "degrades rather than breaking", and it is
   four assertions, not a hope.
5. **Unparsed status lines.** *Test:* "a status line the parser did not understand is shown verbatim
   below the allowances"; "no such lines means no footnote at all".
6. **The trigger.** *Test:* `AppHeader` gains its first unit test — "the faction name is a button that
   says whether the panel is open" (`aria-expanded`), and "there is no faction chip when no report is
   loaded". Then wire `AppShell`.
7. **Smoke.** *Tests:* in `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`, beside the merged-factions tests at `:202`
   and the Escape test at `:1695` — "the faction chip opens the faction view"; "the faction view
   closes on Escape"; "the faction view closes on an outside press"; "a merged ally is marked in the
   attitude list"; "the faction view survives a reload" (see the traps — a restored turn must still
   populate it).

## The test plan

Unit (vitest, `renderToStaticMarkup`, string/regex assertions):

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/factionView.test.ts` — increments 1 and 2 above. This is where the
  0-of-0 case, the `none.` level and the merged-id matching are pinned.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/FactionPanel.test.tsx` — increments 3, 4 and 5: content, the four
  degradation cases, and the unparsed footnote.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.test.tsx` — new file; the trigger and its `aria-expanded`.

Browser (`tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`, Playwright, assertions in the house style
`await expect(page.getByTestId("…")).toContainText(…)` with whitespace-tolerant regexes): increment 7.
Interaction is only ever proved here — `renderToStaticMarkup` cannot click anything, and zustand
serves initial state to a server snapshot (the note at `LayerChips.test.tsx:31-35`).

Suites that must run: `pnpm test`, then `pnpm check` before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

Mockup: **`docs/ui/faction-view.html`** (merged as PR #170), drawn against the real
`tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep` — Borg TNG (95), Magic 5, 6,038 unclaimed
silver, `Regions 0 (0)`, `Mages 6 (6)`, `Apprentices 15 (15)`, and 32 declared factions across five
levels. That last figure is what the three placements were judged on.

- **Placement: a popover anchored off the faction name in the header**, in the shape
  `MergedFactionsPanel` and `TurnMessagesPanel` already use, dismissed on Escape and on an outside
  press, with the attitude list scrolling inside it. Rejected: a sixth collapsible dock panel — a
  19rem column is the worst shape for 32 names, and every existing panel is hex- or unit-scoped; and a
  centred dialog, which blocks the map for something read at a glance.
- **Attitudes: a line per level** — the report's own shape, level label on the left, the factions run
  together as prose. Rejected: a row per faction, and chips under a heading.
- **A level the report prints as `none.` is shown as declared-and-empty**, not omitted. The report
  states it, so the view states it.
- **Allowances: a bar with the number beside it, lit brass when used equals maximum**, so "there is no
  room for another apprentice" reads without arithmetic. Rejected: numbers only, and plain numbers with
  no emphasis.
- **A merged faction is marked in brass with a `⌂` glyph**, so the mark survives being read without
  colour. Rejected: brass alone, and a trailing "— merged".
- **Status lines the parser did not understand are shown verbatim, dimmed, below the allowances.**
  The parser keeps them deliberately; showing them means the app never silently discards something the
  report stated.

## Out of scope

- Writing or editing `DECLARE` orders. This view reads; the grammar at
  `crates/core/src/orders/grammar.rs:68` is untouched.
- How attitudes or allowances changed since last turn — that is `ah-jg6`.
- Making a faction name clickable, linking to a merged faction's report, or any navigation out of the
  view. It marks a merged faction and stops there; the bead says not to invent links to factions the
  app knows nothing about.
- Any faction statistic the report does not state.
- Extracting the five-way duplicated popover-dismiss effect (`MergedFactionsPanel:27`,
  `TurnMessagesPanel:44`, `ProblemsPanel:32`, `GamePicker:48`, `ExportMenu:41`) into a shared hook. It
  is a real duplication and worth its own bead; doing it here would put a refactor of four working
  surfaces inside a feature PR.
- Persisting whether the view was open. The other header popovers do not, and this is read
  occasionally.
- Sorting or interpreting the attitude levels. They appear in the order the report printed them.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm test
pnpm check
```

By hand: import `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep`, open the faction view from
the header, and read it against the report text at lines 42–52 and 1934–1950 — Borg TNG (95), Magic 5,
6,038 unclaimed silver, `Regions 0 / 0`, `Mages 6 / 6` lit, `Apprentices 15 / 15` lit, default
Unfriendly, `Unfriendly` present but empty, `Fon (8)` the only Neutral, and `Heirs of the Sun (90)`
last in the Hostile line. Then merge the f73 report in and confirm **Cone's Magicians (73)** picks up
the merged mark in the Ally line. Then import an older or smaller report that carries neither block and
confirm the view still opens.

Only a human can judge the last part: whether 32 names in a 20rem popover is genuinely readable at the
real font size, and whether the scroll region lands in a sensible place.

## Known traps

- **`ah-vp3.1` must be merged first, and its field names are the authority.** Its own plan flags that
  serde does not propagate `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` into nested structs, so a field can
  arrive as `default_attitude` while the hand-written mirror says `defaultAttitude` — and TypeScript
  cannot catch it, because the mirror is hand-written. It reads `undefined` at runtime. Confirm against
  the merged mirror in `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` and against a real parsed fixture, not
  against this plan.
- **The faction trigger needs its own `relative` wrapper.** The merged-factions chip already lives
  inside the `relative` span around the faction name (`AppHeader.tsx:218-240`), and the popover
  dismissal test is `panelRef.current?.parentElement.contains(target)`. Two popovers sharing one
  parent means pressing the merged chip counts as *inside* the faction panel and fails to dismiss it —
  and vice versa. Give the faction trigger and its panel a `relative` span of their own, sibling to the
  merged chip's.
- **`onDragOver={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}` on the panel root.** The header is the drop target for
  report files. A floating panel without this quietly becomes one, and dropping a report on it does
  nothing visible.
- **`whitespace-normal` on the panel.** The header sets `whitespace-nowrap`, which a child inherits —
  omit it and the 13-name Ally line becomes one enormous horizontal scroll.
- **A restored turn must populate the view.** `parsed` is React state, not store state, and the report
  is re-parsed from stored raw text on reload. Check that the header survives that path — `gameMemory`
  is where a turn is restored from — or the view is empty after every reload while looking fine on
  import. The smoke test in increment 7 is what catches this.
- **`Regions: 0 (0)` is real.** A naive `used / maximum` divides by zero and renders `NaN%` into a
  style attribute, which fails silently rather than loudly. Increment 1 exists for this.
- **Faction ids are strings** in `FactionRef` (`{ name: string; id: string }`), and
  `MergedReportRecord.mergedFactionId` may not be. Compare like with like; `"73" !== 73` will simply
  never mark anything, with no error.
- **`AppHeader` has no unit test today** — nor do `MergedFactionsPanel` or `TurnMessagesPanel`. You are
  writing the first one. Do not assume a test helper exists for rendering the header; build the props
  by hand as the other component tests do.
- **Adding a required prop to `AppHeaderProps` breaks nothing at compile time if it is optional** — make
  the three new props required, so the shell is forced to wire them and the typecheck says so.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — another agent usually holds it in a worktree. `git fetch origin main`
  and branch from `origin/main`.
- **Ignore `.claude/worktrees/`** when grepping; they are full duplicate checkouts of other agents'
  in-flight branches.
acceptance_criteria: A faction view shows the faction name, id and types, the unclaimed silver, the status counts as used-of-maximum, and the declared attitudes grouped by level with the default stated; a merged-in faction is marked as such in the attitude lists; a report lacking either block degrades rather than breaking; the surface is the one the navigator chose, and the chosen mockup is committed under docs/ui/

title: Parse faction status and declared attitudes, and carry them to TypeScript
description:
## Summary

The reading half of ah-vp3: get the `Faction Status:` and `Declared Attitudes:` blocks out of the
report preamble and across the boundary, so a view can be built on them. No UI.

## Why this is its own bead

ah-vp3 spans a Rust parser, two adapters, a hand-written TypeScript mirror and a new faction view
whose shape the navigator has still to choose. The parsing half needs no design decision and can be
proved entirely against the committed fixtures; the view is a separate session with mockups.

## What the report says

    Faction Status:
    Regions: 3 (10)
    Quartermasters: 0 (0)
    Mages: 6 (6)
    Apprentices: 0 (15)

    Declared Attitudes (default Unfriendly):
    Hostile : Creatures (2), The Guardsmen (1), Dark League (28),
      Gyperboreya (42), ...
    Unfriendly : none.
    Neutral : Fon (8).

## Scope

- Parse both blocks in `crates/core/src/report/header.rs`, key-agnostic for the status block
  (NewOrigins prints `Regions`, standard Atlantis prints `Tax Regions` and `Trade Regions`) and
  carrying an unrecognised line rather than dropping it.
- Extend `ReportHeader` and carry the new fields through `crates/core-wasm` and `crates/core-tauri`,
  which serialise straight through, and through the hand-written mirror in
  `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`.
- Stay tolerant: a report without either block parses and leaves the fields empty.

## Out of scope

- Any UI. That is the sibling bead.
- DECLARE orders, and turn-on-turn change tracking (ah-jg6).
design:
## Context

`parse_header` names `"Faction Status"` only to skip it (`crates/core/src/report/header.rs:151`) and
never looks at `Declared Attitudes` at all. Both blocks sit in the preamble slice `parse_header`
already receives (everything before the first region block, `crates/core/src/report/mod.rs:94`), so
the boundary of the slice needs no change — only the parser inside it.

This is the reading half of the epic ah-vp3. When it lands, `ReportHeaderInfo` carries the faction's
allowances and its declared attitudes, and the sibling bead ah-vp3.2 can build a view on them. No UI
here.

The real text, from the committed fixtures:

    Faction Status:                      Declared Attitudes (default Unfriendly):
    Regions: 0 (0)                       Hostile : Creatures (2), The Guardsmen (1), Dark League (28),
    Quartermasters: 0 (0)                  Gyperboreya (42), ... Heirs of the Sun (90).
    Mages: 6 (6)                         Unfriendly : none.
    Apprentices: 15 (15)                 Neutral : Fon (8).

f73 turn 71 has `Regions: 3 (10)`, `Apprentices: 0 (15)`, `default Neutral` and a single
`Ally : Borg TNG (95).`; f73 turn 2 has `Unfriendly : Creatures (2).`

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`crates/core/src/report/header.rs`** — the parsing, and the new types beside `ReportHeader`:

  ```rust
  pub struct FactionStatus { entries: Vec<FactionStatusEntry>, unparsed: Vec<String> }
  pub struct FactionStatusEntry { label: String, used: i64, maximum: i64 }
  pub struct DeclaredAttitudes { default_attitude: Option<String>, levels: Vec<AttitudeLevel> }
  pub struct AttitudeLevel { attitude: String, factions: Vec<FactionRef> }
  pub struct FactionRef { name: String, id: String }
  ```

  Both new fields on `ReportHeader` are plain structs deriving `Default`, not `Option`: a report
  without either block leaves them empty, which is what "degrade rather than break" means for a
  consumer. `entries` is key-agnostic — the label is whatever the ruleset printed, so NewOrigins'
  `Regions` and standard Atlantis' `Tax Regions` / `Trade Regions` both work with no list of known
  keys. A status line that is not `Label: n (m)` goes to `unparsed` rather than being dropped.
  Levels are kept in the order the report prints them, `none.` included as an empty list — the
  report states them, so the view can too.
- **`crates/core/src/report/scan.rs`** — reuse, do not reinvent: `is_none_list` (`:181`) for
  `none.`, `split_top_level(input, ',')` (`:13`) for the faction list, and `split_trailing_id`
  (`:45`) for `Creatures (2)`. All three already exist for exactly these shapes.
- **`crates/core/src/report/header.rs`**'s `Section` enum gains `FactionStatus` and `Attitudes`.
  `"Faction Status"` currently appears in the arm that sets `Section::None` (`:151`) and moves to
  setting `Section::FactionStatus`.
- **`crates/core/tests/parse_real_reports.rs`** — the fixture assertions live here (unclaimed silver
  at `:197` and `:207` are the pattern to follow).
- **`crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:648`** and **`crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:458`** — both serialise
  `ParsedReport` straight through, so neither needs a change *provided the new structs carry their
  own serde attribute*; see the traps.
- **`packages/core-client/src/index.ts:391`** — `ReportHeaderInfo`, the one hand-written mirror.
  Add the five types and the two fields.
- **`packages/browser-core/src/parseReportFull.test.ts`** — where the boundary is actually proved,
  against the real fixture through wasm.

**No persistence change.** `crates/core-persistence` holds no header columns and the report is
re-parsed from its stored raw text, so nothing here touches the schema or its seven migrations.

## Increments

1. **Confirm the wrapping, first.** RED: a `header.rs` unit test parsing a `Hostile :` line whose
   entries wrap over three physical lines, asserting the *last* faction on the last physical line is
   present. `unwrap_lines` joins a continuation only when it is more indented **and** the first word
   would not have fitted in the wrap column (`crates/core/src/report/unwrap.rs:93-98`), so whether
   the parser sees one logical line is a fact about real text, not an assumption. If it turns out
   not to join, the parser accumulates continuation lines itself and the rest of the plan is
   unchanged — find that out here, in the cheapest place, rather than against a fixture.
2. **The attitudes block.** RED: `reads the declared attitudes` — default attitude, one level per
   printed line, `none.` as an empty list. GREEN: `Section::Attitudes` and the parsing.
3. **The status block.** RED: `reads the faction status as used of maximum` plus
   `keeps a status line it does not understand` and `does not care what the keys are called`
   (`Tax Regions: 3 (10)`). GREEN: `Section::FactionStatus`.
4. **The real reports.** RED: assertions in `parse_real_reports.rs` for f95 t71, f73 t71 and f73 t2.
   GREEN: whatever 1-3 got wrong about real text.
5. **The boundary.** RED: `parseReportFull.test.ts` expects `header.attitudes.levels` and
   `header.factionStatus.entries` on the parsed fixture. GREEN: the TypeScript mirror, and the serde
   attributes that make the names match.

## The test plan

Suites: `cargo test -p atlantis-core` while the parsing is being written, then
`cargo test --workspace` and `pnpm -r run test`. `pnpm run check` before the PR.

`crates/core/src/report/header.rs` unit tests, beside the existing ones at `:209`:
- `joins a wrapped attitude line` — increment 1, and the only test whose failure changes the design.
- `reads the declared attitudes` — default, five levels in printed order, ids and names split.
- `reads an attitude level of none as an empty list` — `Unfriendly : none.` yields the level with no
  factions, not a missing level.
- `reads the faction status as used of maximum`.
- `does not care what the status keys are called` — `Tax Regions: 3 (10)`, `Trade Regions: 1 (4)`.
- `keeps a status line it does not understand` — carried in `unparsed`, and the block's other lines
  still parse.
- `parses a report with neither block` — both fields empty, and everything else in the header
  unaffected. This is the tolerance contract.
- `does not swallow the unclaimed silver line` — see the traps; a status block followed by
  `Unclaimed silver: 6038.` must still set `unclaimed_silver`, and must not add an entry called
  "Unclaimed silver".

`crates/core/tests/parse_real_reports.rs`:
- f95 t71: `Regions 0 (0)`, `Mages 6 (6)`, `Apprentices 15 (15)`, default `Unfriendly`, `Fon (8)`
  the only Neutral, and the Hostile level ending in `Heirs of the Sun (90)` — that last one is the
  wrapped-entry proof against real text.
- f73 t71: `Regions 3 (10)`, `Apprentices 0 (15)`, default `Neutral`, `Ally` holding only
  `Borg TNG (95)`.
- f73 t2: `Unfriendly` holding `Creatures (2)`, everything else empty.

`packages/browser-core/src/parseReportFull.test.ts`:
- assert the two new fields on the parsed f95 fixture, by their **camelCase** names, with one real
  value each. This is the only test that can catch a serde naming mismatch, and it is the reason
  increment 5 is a test rather than a type declaration.

## User-facing decisions

None. This bead stops at the boundary and shows nothing. The surface that will display all of it is
the sibling bead **ah-vp3.2**, which is blocked on this one and needs the navigator and a mockup
before it can be planned — the parent ah-vp3 proposes an anchored panel off the header's
`Faction <name>`, in the shape `TurnMessagesPanel` and `MergedFactionsPanel` already use, but that is
a proposal and explicitly not decided.

## Out of scope

- Any UI, chip, panel or rendering. ah-vp3.2.
- `DECLARE` orders. The grammar at `crates/core/src/orders/grammar.rs:68` is the writing side and is
  untouched.
- Turn-on-turn change tracking for attitudes or allowances — ah-jg6.
- Any faction statistic the report does not state.
- The persistence schema, which holds no header data.
- Interpreting attitudes: no sorting into a "friendliness" order, no inferring an attitude for a
  faction the report does not list. The default attitude is reported, not applied.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-core
cargo test --workspace
pnpm -r run test
pnpm run check
```

Manually, against `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-f95-t71.rep` read side by side with a
debug print or a test assertion: 6 of 6 mages, 15 of 15 apprentices, `Regions 0 (0)`, default
Unfriendly, `Fon (8)` neutral. Nothing to click — the view arrives with ah-vp3.2.

## Known traps

- **A nested struct needs its own `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`.** `ParsedReport` carries the
  attribute at `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:648`, but serde does not propagate it into nested types:
  `default_attitude` would cross the boundary as `default_attitude` while the hand-written mirror
  says `defaultAttitude`, and TypeScript cannot catch it because the mirror is hand-written. The
  field simply reads `undefined` at runtime. Every new struct carries the attribute, and increment 5
  is what proves it.
- **The `Unclaimed silver:` line is `Label: n` shaped.** The existing branch for it (`:192`) is
  checked *before* the `match section`, exactly as the errors and events branches are. The new
  section capture must stay after those specific branches, or a status block that runs on into the
  silver line eats it and `unclaimed_silver` goes quietly null — with the existing fixture assertion
  at `parse_real_reports.rs:197` as the only thing standing in the way. Keep that assertion; do not
  "fix" it.
- **Where the block ends is not marked.** `unwrap_lines` drops blank lines, so the parser cannot see
  the blank line that separates the blocks in the source. End each section on the first line that
  does not match its shape, as well as on the section headers `parse_header` already recognises. A
  section that runs to the end of the preamble swallows the errors and events lists.
- **`unwrap_lines` may or may not join the wrapped attitude entries.** Its rule is
  more-indented *and* the first word would not have fitted (`unwrap.rs:93-98`). Increment 1 exists
  to settle this before anything is built on the answer.
- **Adding a required field to `ReportHeaderInfo` breaks three object literals** —
  `packages/shared/src/orderDraft.test.ts:23`, `hexMapModel.test.ts:109` and `gameMemory.test.ts:51`
  each build a whole header by hand. They must be updated; the typecheck will say so, but only after
  the mirror changes, so expect it rather than reading it as a mistake.
- **`Hostile : ` has a space before the colon**, and every entry list ends in a full stop. Split on
  the first `:` and trim both sides; strip the trailing `.` before splitting on commas, or the last
  faction's id arrives as `90).`
- **A faction name can contain a comma or brackets.** Use `split_top_level`, which respects nesting,
  not `str::split(',')` — the helper exists for this.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — another agent usually holds it in a worktree. Branch from
  `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria: The Faction Status block parses into ordered used-of-maximum entries, key-agnostic, with an unrecognised key carried rather than dropped; the Declared Attitudes block parses into the default attitude plus the factions declared at each level, with wrapped entries and 'none.' handled; both are exposed through the wasm and Tauri adapters and mirrored in packages/core-client; a report missing either block still parses with the fields empty; the f95 and f73 turn-71 fixtures are asserted against real values

title: The release tag lands on a bead-export commit, not the release commit
description:
## Summary

`v0.5.3` released successfully — the first release since ah-7go, and the first that reached a tag at
all — but the tag does not point at the release commit:

```
b757b1d chore(beads): refresh the issues export   <- v0.5.3 points here
81410b3 chore(beads): refresh the issues export
9bbf5c2 chore(beads): refresh the issues export
c24a8ba Release v0.5.3                            <- where the tag belongs
```

Three export refreshes landed between the release commit and its tag. The built artifacts are still
right, since `b757b1d` is a descendant of the bump and carries the same manifests, but the tag no
longer names the commit it is a tag for — which was the stated point of settling the export first.

## Why the ah-7go fix is not enough

ah-7go settles the bead export **before** the bump, so the gate has nothing to do when the release
pushes. That holds only if the database stops changing for the duration of the release, and it does
not: several agents claim, close and label beads continuously, and a release run takes minutes
because of its own local quality gate.

So the export goes stale again between the settle and the release push. The gate then fires on that
push, commits a refresh and aborts, and the retry walks past it — repeatedly, once per agent that
touched a bead in the meantime. Each retry adds a commit, and the tag ends up on whichever refresh
happened to be last.

The gate is behaving exactly as designed. The release is what has to stop being surprised by it.

## Scope

- Make the tag point at the `Release vX.Y.Z` commit, whatever the gate does around it.
- Options to weigh when the bead is worked, none of them decided:
  1. **Tag before pushing.** Create the tag on the release commit locally, then push the branch and
     the tag. The gate may still add commits on top; the tag stays where it belongs.
  2. **Push with the gate stood down for that one push.** The export was settled seconds earlier and
     is stale only because of unrelated bead traffic; the release does not need to carry it.
  3. **Re-point the tag after the pushes settle.** Simplest to write, worst to read: a tag that
     moves is a tag nobody trusts.
- Whatever is chosen, the release must still end tagged and pushed with a stale export, which is the
  ah-7go acceptance criterion and must not regress.

## Out of scope

- The export gate's own behaviour. Its "push again" contract is deliberate and documented.
- The main ruleset.

## Validation

- A release run on a database that changes mid-run — claim or close a bead from another session
  while the release's quality gate is running — ends with the tag on the `Release vX.Y.Z` commit.
- `git ls-remote --tags origin` and `git log` agree about which commit the tag names.
- The existing ah-7go behaviour still holds: a stale export at the start does not strand the run.
design: Found by inspecting v0.5.3, the first release after ah-7go. That fix settles the export before the bump, which assumes the database is quiet for the rest of the run - and with several agents claiming and closing beads while the release's own quality gate runs for minutes, it is not. The export goes stale again, the gate fires on the release push, and the retry walks the tag onto whichever refresh commit landed last.
acceptance_criteria:
A release run whose bead database changes mid-run ends with the tag on the Release vX.Y.Z commit.
git ls-remote --tags origin and git log agree about which commit the tag names.
A release that starts with a stale export still ends tagged and pushed, as ah-7go requires.
notes:
Blocked on ah-r2e (2026-08-13, planning session), and not planned yet on purpose.

Both beads rewrite the same few lines of scripts/release.ts: ah-r2e routes all three pushes through
a bounded retry and adds a recovery message, and this bead changes where the tag is created relative
to those pushes. Planning this one first would specify it against code ah-r2e is about to replace,
and implementing them in parallel would conflict in one file.

There is also a substantive reason to wait for the measurement. ah-r2e's root-cause half normalizes
the volatile lease fields (heartbeat_at, lease_expires_at) out of the committed export, and those
are the only fields a bd heartbeat touches - one export churn per active claim per minute. Much of
the traffic that put three refresh commits between the release commit and its tag was that churn
rather than real bead changes. So once ah-r2e lands, re-measure before choosing between this bead's
three options: the remaining churn may be small enough that "tag before pushing" is plainly the
right answer and needs no argument.

title: A view for reading the turn's battles
description:
## Summary

A view that lists the battles of the loaded turn and shows one in full.

## Problem

Once ah-1is.1 lands, the battles are in the model and still nowhere on screen.

## Scope

- A list of the turn's battles, each line answering who fought whom, where, and the outcome in
  casualties, so a player can see at a glance whether the turn went well.
- Opening one shows it in full: both rosters, the rounds in order with their spells and loss
  lines, total casualties, damaged units and the spoils.
- The location links back to the map — selecting a battle should be able to take the player to
  the hex it happened in, the way the turn-messages panel takes them to a unit
  (`onSelectUnit`, `packages/shared/src/workspace/TurnMessagesPanel.tsx:39`).
- Units that are the player's own should be distinguishable from everyone else's in the
  rosters. The parsed unit model already carries `own`
  (`crates/core/src/report/model.rs:104-107`) for units in regions; if the battle roster does not
  give enough to decide, match on faction id and say plainly when it cannot be told.
- Round statistics arrive as text (see ah-1is.1). Show them, but folded away by default — they
  are hundreds of lines and would bury the rounds themselves.

**Shape.** Every faction- or turn-scoped surface today is a header chip with a popover
(`TurnMessagesPanel`, `ProblemsPanel`, `MergedFactionsPanel`, mounted from
`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx:2027-2105`); all five collapsible panels are
hex- or unit-scoped. A battle in full is much larger than any of those popovers hold, so this
one probably wants a chip that opens something bigger — a dialog, or a list in the popover that
opens the full battle elsewhere. Put the options to the navigator before building, as the
faction view bead (ah-vp3) does.

## Out of scope

- Anything the parser does not provide (see ah-1is.1: round statistics stay as text).
- Comparing battles across turns.

## Validation

- `pnpm test` — component tests over the list and the full view, including a turn with no
  battles.
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`
- A smoke test in `tests/smoke/` covering opening a battle from the header, in the style of the
  existing turn-messages coverage.
- Manual: import `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-f95-t71.rep`, open the second battle
  (`Sail (16352)` attacks `Looter (16779)` in `ocean (26,52)`), and check the casualties and
  spoils against the report text.
design:
## Context

ah-1is.1 landed the parser: `ParsedReport.battles` now carries every battle of the turn - headline,
attacker and defender, terrain/coordinate/province, both rosters, the rounds with their lines,
spells and loss lines, the round and battle statistics as text, total casualties, damaged units and
spoils (`packages/core-client/src/index.ts:415-476`). Nothing shows any of it. A player who fought
this turn still has to open the raw report, and in the turn-71 fixture the battles are 75 KB of a
199 KB file.

What the real data looks like, and what it forces:

- **Two battles**, both in `neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep`. The first is `AA Tomb's Guards (7280)
  attacks Pirates (14789) in ocean (25,55)` with **158 units on the attacker roster and one
  defender**; the second is `Sail (16352) attacks Looter (16779) in ocean (26,52)` with a comparable
  roster. **One round each.**
- The player's own faction appears **inside the attacker's allied army**, not as the attacker:
  `Borg TNG (95)` occurs 24 times in the section, on lines like
  `One of Eight (18636), Borg TNG (95), behind, leader [LEAD], …`.
- Many roster lines print **no faction at all** (`Ailen's Acolyte (2965), behind, leader [LEAD], …`),
  so those units cannot be attributed to anyone.

When this lands, a player can see at a glance whether the turn's fighting went well, read any battle
in full, and get from a battle to the hex it happened in.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/BattlesDialog.tsx`** - new. The whole surface: the list rail and
  the battle detail. Model it on `MapExportDialog.tsx` - `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`
  (`:76-77`), and `useEscapeToDismiss(onDismiss)` from `./dismissLayer`, which is the *only* correct
  way to close on Escape here; it registers on the dismiss stack so a dialog under a newer palette
  does not steal the key.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/battles.ts`** - new, and where the thinking goes. Pure functions
  over `Battle[]`: the one-line summary for a list row (participants, hex label, attacker and
  defender losses, whether there are spoils), whether a roster entry is the viewer's own, and the
  counts a roster heading shows. Keeping it out of the component is what makes it testable without a
  DOM - see the traps.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx`** - a `Battles` chip beside `problemCount` /
  `problemsPanel` (`:64-68`, rendered `:317-334`). Follow the problems chip exactly: **the chip is
  absent when the turn has no battles**, as `problemCount > 0` already does. The dialog itself is
  *not* a header child - see below.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`** - `parsed` is the `ParsedReport` (`:256`), so
  `parsed.battles` is already in hand and nothing new needs loading. Add `battlesOpen` state beside
  `problemsOpen`, pass the count and toggle into `AppHeader`, and render `<BattlesDialog>` **beside
  `<MapExportDialog>` at `:2267`**, not inside the header - the header's popovers are anchored to
  their chips, and this is a centred dialog over the workspace. Reuse `selectHex` (`:445`) for "show
  on map", `hexLabel` (`:481`) for the list line's hex, and `parsed.header.factionId` for deciding
  whose units are whose.
- **`packages/shared/src/navigationGuide.ts`** - the guide lists every way into a surface
  (`:179` is the problems entry). Add the battles one in the same voice.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/CommandPalette.tsx`** / the command list at `AppShell.tsx:708` -
  an `Open battles` command, present only when the turn has battles, exactly as `export-map` is
  present only when `parsed`.
- **Tests**: `packages/shared/src/workspace/battles.test.ts` (new, pure), a markup test in the style
  of `BadgeMenu.test.tsx`, and a walk in `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` beside the turn-messages
  coverage.
- **Nothing in `crates/`.** The parser is done and this bead adds no field to it. If something turns
  out to be missing from the model, that is a finding for a new bead, not a change here.

## User-facing decisions

Both settled with the navigator on 2026-08-13, drawn as three candidates in
**`docs/ui/battles-view.html`** (committed by PR #166, merged).

1. **Where the view lives: candidate B - the chip opens one dialog, with the battle list down a
   narrow left rail (~19rem) and the selected battle filling the rest.** Opening the chip selects
   the first battle, so the dialog is never empty; moving between battles is one click and the
   summaries stay on screen as context. A was rejected because a popover→dialog pair costs two
   clicks and throws the list away; C (a sixth collapsible panel) because at ~22rem the rosters
   cannot sit side by side and a 158-unit roster reads as an endless column.
2. **A list line states its outcome neutrally: `attacker −0 · defender −15`, not "we" and "they".**
   In turn 71 the player's units fight inside an allied army whose attacker belongs to another
   faction, and some roster lines print no faction at all, so "we" would be a guess and casualties
   are reported per unit-group rather than per faction anyway. Whose units were there is answered
   where it can be: in the rosters, which mark the player's own units and count them
   (`Attackers 158 · 12 yours`), and which mark a unit whose faction is not printed as unknown
   rather than as somebody else's.

The mockup also draws, and the navigator saw: the hex on the list line and a "show on map" link in
the battle head; rosters side by side; rounds with their loss lines; the outcome as casualties,
damaged units and spoils; and both statistics blocks folded behind a disclosure that says how many
lines it holds. Build what the page shows.

## Increments

Each opens with a failing test. `pnpm test` between them; `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck` before the
PR.

1. **The list line.** RED: `battles.test.ts` - `summarise(battle, hexLabel)` over the turn-71
   fixture's two battles returns attacker and defender as printed, the hex label, attacker losses 0
   and defender losses 15 for the first, and that it has spoils. Also a battle whose headline was
   not recognised (`attacker === null`): the summary falls back to the verbatim headline rather than
   rendering an empty line.
2. **Whose unit is whose.** RED: `allegianceOf(unit, viewerFactionId)` returns `"own"` for
   `One of Eight (18636), Borg TNG (95)`, `"other"` for `AA Tomb's Guards (7280), Greywolf (33)`,
   and `"unknown"` for `Ailen's Acolyte (2965)`, which prints no faction. Then the roster counts:
   158 attackers, 12 of them the viewer's, on the turn-71 first battle - read the real number out of
   the fixture rather than trusting this one.
3. **The list rail, as markup.** RED: a `BattlesDialog.test.tsx` in the `BadgeMenu.test.tsx` style -
   `renderToStaticMarkup` and assert both battles appear, the first is marked selected, each line
   carries its hex and its losses, and the dialog has `role="dialog"` and an accessible name.
4. **The battle in full, as markup.** Both rosters with their headings and counts, own units marked,
   the round's lines and loss lines, casualties, damaged units and spoils. Assert the statistics
