   blocks are **present but collapsed** - a `<details>` without `open`, or an equivalent that a
   markup test can see - and that the disclosure says how many lines it holds.
5. **The empty state.** A turn with no battles: the chip is absent from the header entirely (assert
   through `AppHeader`, as the problems chip is), and the dialog, if rendered directly, says so
   plainly rather than drawing an empty rail.
6. **Wiring.** `AppShell` state, the chip, the dialog beside `MapExportDialog`, the command-palette
   entry and the navigation-guide line. Covered by the smoke walk rather than by a unit test.
7. **The smoke walk.** In `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`, after `loadReport`: open the battles chip,
   expect the dialog with two battles listed, expect the first battle's rosters and its spoils,
   select the second battle and expect `Sail (16352)`/`Looter (16779)` and `271 silver`, expand the
   battle statistics and expect a statistics line, then use "show on map" and expect the region panel
   to follow to `(26,52)`. Escape closes it.

## The test plan

**`packages/shared/src/workspace/battles.test.ts`** - the pure layer, against the real fixture text
parsed through the core rather than hand-built objects where that is practical: the list summary
(participants, hex, attacker/defender losses, spoils), the unrecognised-headline fallback, the
three-way allegiance, and the roster counts.

**`packages/shared/src/workspace/BattlesDialog.test.tsx`** - markup only (`renderToStaticMarkup`):
the rail lists every battle with its outcome, the selected battle renders both rosters with counts
and own-unit marks, the rounds and the outcome are present, both statistics blocks are present and
collapsed, and the no-battles state says so.

**`tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`** - one walk, described in increment 7. This is where clicking,
selection, disclosure and dismissal are proved, because the repository has no jsdom.

Suites that must run: `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm run test:smoke`, and
`pnpm run check` before the PR.

## Out of scope

- Any parser change. Round statistics stay as text - that is ah-1is.1's decision, and this bead
  shows them folded rather than modelling them.
- Comparing battles across turns, or a battle history: this is the loaded turn's battles only.
- Anything to do with an ally's report of the same battle, or merging two accounts of one fight.
- Assessing or scoring a battle - no won/lost verdict, which the report never states.
- Making a battle's units selectable on the map. The bead asks that the *location* link back; a unit
  in a roster may not exist in the loaded turn at all, and `goToUnit` only knows units the turn
  describes. If a roster unit happens to be a known unit, linking it is a nice-to-have and a
  separate bead, not this one.
- Persisting which battle was last read.

## Validation

```
pnpm test
pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check
```

Manual, and worth doing once: import `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep`, open
the second battle (`Sail (16352)` attacks `Looter (16779)` in `ocean (26,52)`), and check the
casualties (`Looter (16779) loses 1`, `Sail (16352) loses 0`, damaged `16779`) and the spoils
(`mithril sword`, `mithril armor`, `2 giant turtles`, `271 silver`) against the report text at lines
1466-1473. Also confirm by eye that the 158-unit roster scrolls inside its own column rather than
pushing the outcome off the bottom of the dialog.

## Known traps

- **There is no jsdom in this repository.** Component tests render to static markup with
  `renderToStaticMarkup` and assert on the string (`BadgeMenu.test.tsx` says so in its own doc
  comment). A test that tries to click, toggle or focus will not run - that work belongs in
  `tests/smoke/`. This is why increments 1 and 2 put the logic in `battles.ts` rather than in the
  component.
- **Escape must go through `useEscapeToDismiss`** (`workspace/dismissLayer.ts`), never a bare
  `keydown` listener. The listener is captured and gated on the dismiss stack so that Escape closes
  only the topmost surface; a hand-rolled one closes this dialog from under the command palette.
- **The dialog is not a header child.** `TurnMessagesPanel` documents why the header's popovers
  stop `dragover`: the header is the only element that accepts a dropped report, and a floating
  child of it becomes an invisible drop target over the map. Rendering this beside `MapExportDialog`
  in the workspace avoids that inheritance entirely - do not be tempted to hang it off the chip.
- **"Own" cannot always be told.** Three states, not two: the faction id matches the viewer's, it is
  some other faction, or the line prints no faction. Rendering the third as "not yours" is wrong and
  the bead says to say plainly when it cannot be told.
- **The rosters are big.** 158 entries in the fixture, each with a body that can run to a paragraph.
  Give each roster its own scroll container and keep the body on one line with an ellipsis, as the
  mockup draws it; letting the dialog grow means the outcome and spoils - the part a player came
  for - end up below the fold.
- **The statistics blocks are the bulk of the report.** 17 lines per round and 44 for the battle in
  the fixture, and a longer battle has one per round. Collapsed by default is a requirement, not a
  preference, and the disclosure should say how many lines are behind it.
- **WebKit's driver returns `""` for text it considers clipped**, so a smoke assertion on text
  inside a scrolled roster can pass in Chromium and fail in the native shell. Assert on things
  visible without scrolling - the headline, the counts, the outcome - and scroll deliberately before
  asserting on anything deeper.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled**, so a `test:pwa` run
  straight after `test:smoke` fails with timeouts that look like a broken worker. Run
  `pnpm run check`, which orders them correctly.
- **A battle's coordinate can be `null`** when the headline was not recognised, and its hex may be
  one the map has never heard of - the turn-71 battles are in ocean hexes the faction sailed
  through. "Show on map" must degrade to nothing rather than selecting a hex that does not exist;
  `hexLabel` (`AppShell.tsx:481`) already answers for an unexplored region id and is the right thing
  to lean on.
acceptance_criteria: The turn's battles are listed with participants, location and casualties; opening one shows both rosters, the rounds in order, total casualties, damaged units and spoils; the battle's hex can be reached from the view; round statistics are available but folded away by default; a turn with no battles shows an empty state rather than breaking

title: Parse the battles of the turn report
description:
## Summary

Parse the `Battles during turn:` section into a structured model and expose it to the
TypeScript side, so a view can be built on it.

## Problem

The section is skipped outright (`crates/core/src/report/header.rs:151`). Nothing downstream
can see a battle.

## Scope

**Where it goes.** The battles sit inside the preamble slice `parse_header` is given —
everything before the first region block (`crates/core/src/report/mod.rs:94`) — and today's
real-report tests pass, which proves no battle line is mistaken for a region header. Put the
parsing in a new `crates/core/src/report/battle.rs` rather than growing `header.rs`, and have
`parse_header` hand the section to it.

**Splitting the section into battles.** `unwrap_lines` drops blank lines
(`crates/core/src/report/unwrap.rs:85`), so blocks cannot be split on them. Split on the
headline instead — `<unit> (<id>) attacks <unit> (<id>) in <terrain> (<x>,<y>) in <province>!` —
and treat everything up to the next headline (or the end of the preamble) as that battle.
Assassinations print a different headline; recognise what is recognisable and keep the rest as
text rather than dropping a block that does not match.

**The model.** Per battle:

- The headline: attacker and defender unit names and ids, and the location as terrain,
  coordinate and province, so the UI can point at the hex on the map.
- Attacker and defender rosters, one entry per unit: name, id, owning faction where printed,
  flags, and the item/skill body. Parsing the body down to individual items is *not* required
  here — a unit line already has a shape `crates/core/src/report/unit.rs` understands, so reuse
  what fits and keep the remainder verbatim rather than inventing a second unit parser.
- The rounds in order: the round's lines (tactics bonuses, spells, "breathes Fire, killing 15")
  and the per-side loss lines that close it.
- Total casualties per side, the damaged-unit ids, and the spoils.
- `line_start`/`line_end` from `LogicalLine` for the block, so the verbatim report text can be
  recovered for display.

**Round statistics.** The `Round N statistics:` blocks are the bulk of the section — hundreds of
per-unit, per-weapon tallies. Keep them as text attached to their round for now; do not model
them field by field. If that turns out to be wanted, it is a separate bead.

**Tolerance.** A report with no battles parses to an empty list. A battle missing a section
(no spoils line, no statistics) parses with that part empty. Nothing here may make a report fail
to parse.

**Boundary.** Add the battles to `ReportHeader` (or alongside it in `ParsedReport` — the
implementer's call, but say which and why in the PR) and mirror the type in
`packages/core-client/src/index.ts` next to `ReportHeaderInfo` (index.ts:391). Both adapters
serialise `ParsedReport` straight through with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`
(`crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:648`, `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:458`), so the hand-written
TypeScript mirror is the only part that can drift.

**Size.** A parsed turn is persisted, so measure what this adds to a stored turn before
finishing. If keeping the statistics text doubles the record, say so on the bead and propose
dropping it to the navigator rather than deciding alone.

## Out of scope

- Any UI. That is the sibling bead.
- Battles from merged allied reports (see the parent, ah-1is).
- Modelling the round statistics field by field.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p atlantis-core` — unit tests over a hand-written minimal battle, plus the real
  fixture `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-f95-t71.rep`: two battles, the first
  `AA Tomb's Guards (7280)` attacking `Pirates (14789)` in `ocean (25,55)` in `Atlantis Ocean`,
  one round, `Pirates (14789) loses 15`, `AA Tomb's Guards (7280) loses 0`, damaged unit 14789,
  and spoils ending `2531 silver [SILV]`.
- A test that the other fixtures, which have no battles, still parse to an empty list and are
  otherwise unchanged.
- `pnpm test && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck` for the boundary types.
design:
## Context

`Battles during turn:` is skipped outright — `parse_header` names it only to set `Section::None`
(`crates/core/src/report/header.rs:151`), so every battle line falls into the catch-all and is
dropped. Nothing downstream can see a battle.

In the f95 turn-71 fixture the section is lines **57 to 1473**, terminated by `Events during turn:`,
and holds two battles. That is **75 KB of a 199 KB report — 38% of it**. Both are ordinary attacks:

    AA Tomb's Guards (7280) attacks Pirates (14789) in ocean (25,55) in Atlantis Ocean!
    Attackers: … Defenders: … Round 1: … <side> loses N.
    Round 1 statistics: … Battle statistics: …
    Total Casualties: / Pirates (14789) loses 15. / Damaged units: 14789. / AA Tomb's Guards (7280) loses 0.
    Spoils: 3 magic crossbows [MXBO], … 2531 silver [SILV].

When this lands, `ParsedReport` carries an ordered list of battles and the sibling view bead can be
built on it. No UI here.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`crates/core/src/report/battle.rs`** — new, holding the model and `parse_battles(&[LogicalLine])`.
- **`crates/core/src/report/mod.rs`** — the preamble slice is already cut at `:93-94`. Call
  `parse_battles(&lines[..preamble_end])` there, as a **second, independent pass over the same
  slice**, and add the result to `ParsedReport` (`:31`).

  This is a deliberate departure from the bead, which suggested `parse_header` hand the section over.
  Two readers over one slice, each ignoring what it does not own, means `header.rs` needs no change
  at all: `Battles during turn` already sets `Section::None` there, so the battle lines are already
  being ignored correctly and the errors/events lists already stop where they should. Coupling the
  two parsers would put a battle-shaped hole in the header's state machine for no gain.
- **`ParsedReport`** gains `battles: Vec<Battle>` beside `header`, `regions` and `orders_template` —
  **not** a field on `ReportHeader`. A battle is an event, not a fact about the faction, and the
  header type is the one mirrored by hand in TypeScript. See the size note below, which is the real
  reason.
- **`crates/core/src/report/scan.rs`** — reuse `split_trailing_id` (`:45`) for `Pirates (14789)`,
  `parse_coordinate` (`:64`) for `(25,55)`, `split_top_level` (`:13`) for the comma lists, and
  `parse_money` (`:173`) where a count is printed.
- **`crates/core/src/report/unit.rs`** — a roster entry is close to a unit line and the bead asks
  that it be reused where it fits. Reuse what parses name, id and the owning faction; keep the rest
  of the body **verbatim** rather than growing a second unit parser. A roster line here can be a
  paragraph of `#a hero/dwarf` repeats, and nothing downstream has asked for it broken down.
- **`crates/core/tests/parse_real_reports.rs`** — the fixture assertions.
- **`packages/core-client/src/index.ts`** — the hand-written mirror, beside `ReportHeaderInfo`
  (`:391`) and `ParsedReport` (`:415`).
- **`crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:648`** / **`crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:458`** — no change needed;
  both serialise `ParsedReport` straight through. See the traps for the one thing that *is* needed.

### The model

```rust
pub struct Battle {
    headline: String,                  // verbatim, always
    attacker: Option<Combatant>, defender: Option<Combatant>,
    terrain: Option<String>, coordinate: Option<Coordinate>, province: Option<String>,
    attackers: Vec<BattleUnit>, defenders: Vec<BattleUnit>,
    rounds: Vec<BattleRound>,
    statistics: Vec<String>,           // the "Battle statistics:" block, verbatim
    casualties: Vec<Casualty>, damaged_units: Vec<String>, spoils: Option<String>,
    line_start: usize, line_end: usize,
}
pub struct Combatant { name: String, id: String }
pub struct BattleUnit { name, id, faction: Option<Combatant>, flags: Vec<String>, body: String }
pub struct BattleRound { number: Option<u32>, lines: Vec<String>, losses: Vec<Casualty>, statistics: Vec<String> }
pub struct Casualty { combatant: Option<Combatant>, lost: Option<i64>, text: String }
```

Every "structured" field is optional or has a verbatim companion. A block the parser does not
recognise is still a `Battle` with its headline and its span, which is what "recognise what is
recognisable and keep the rest" means in practice.

### On size — measured, and it settles the bead's open question

The bead asks for the storage cost to be measured before finishing, and to escalate if keeping the
statistics text doubles a stored turn. Measured, and it does not, because **`ParsedReport` is never
stored**. `imported_turns` holds `raw_report` and `parsed_payload_json`
(`crates/core-persistence/migrations/0002_imported_turns.sql`), and that payload is a
**`ReportParseResult`** — the flat summary of turn header, factions, regions, units, inventories,
messages and warnings (`crates/core/src/lib.rs:186`). The full model is recomputed from the raw text
by `parse_report_full_state(rawReport)` every time it is wanted
(`crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs`, `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts:423`).

So battles on `ParsedReport` cost **nothing on disk** — the bytes are already stored, once, as
report text. The cost is parse time and memory while a turn is open: about 75 KB of retained strings
for this fixture, against a 199 KB report that is already held in full. That is the whole of the
trade, and it is why the statistics stay as text and why nothing needs to go to the navigator.

**The corollary is a hard rule: battles must not be added to `ReportParseResult`.** That type *is*
persisted, per turn, and putting 75 KB of battle text in it would roughly double a stored turn — the
outcome the bead was right to worry about.

## Increments

1. **Split the section into battles.** RED: `finds each battle in the section` over a hand-written
   minimal section with two blocks — only headlines, spans and nothing else asserted. GREEN: the
   section boundaries and the headline split.
2. **The headline.** RED: `reads the attacker, defender and location from the headline`, including
   the wrapped form (`… in\n  Atlantis Ocean!`). GREEN: the headline parse, with the fields optional.
3. **Rosters.** RED: `reads the attacker and defender rosters`, one entry per unit, faction where
   printed, body kept verbatim — assert on a roster line whose body is a paragraph of repeats.
4. **Rounds and their losses.** RED: `reads the rounds in order with the loss lines that close them`.
5. **The close of the battle.** RED: `reads the total casualties, the damaged units and the spoils` —
   note the report interleaves `Damaged units:` *between* the two casualty lines, so do not assume
   order.
6. **The real reports.** RED: the f95 assertions from the bead's validation, plus
   `a report with no battles parses to an empty list` over the other three fixtures.
7. **The boundary.** RED: a `parseReportFull.test.ts` assertion that the parsed f95 fixture has two
   battles and that the first names `Pirates` as defender. GREEN: the TypeScript mirror and the serde
   attributes.

## The test plan

Suites: `cargo test -p atlantis-core`, then `cargo test --workspace` and `pnpm -r run test`.
`pnpm run check` before the PR.

`crates/core/src/report/battle.rs` unit tests, over a hand-written minimal section:
- `finds each battle in the section`, `stops at the section that follows` (an `Events during turn:`
  line after the last battle must not be swallowed).
- `reads the attacker, defender and location from the headline`, and `keeps a headline it does not
  recognise` — an assassination-shaped line still yields a battle carrying its headline and body.
- `reads the attacker and defender rosters`, `keeps a roster body verbatim`.
- `reads the rounds in order with their loss lines`, `keeps the round statistics as text`.
- `reads the total casualties, damaged units and spoils`, with the damaged-units line between the
  two casualty lines as the real report prints it.
- `parses a battle missing its spoils`, `parses a battle with no statistics` — tolerance.
- `records the line span of each battle` — `line_start`/`line_end` come straight off `LogicalLine`
  (`crates/core/src/report/unwrap.rs:30-35`), so the verbatim text can be recovered for display.

`crates/core/tests/parse_real_reports.rs`:
- f95 t71: two battles; the first `AA Tomb's Guards (7280)` attacking `Pirates (14789)` in
  `ocean (25,55)` in `Atlantis Ocean`; one round; `Pirates (14789) loses 15` and
  `AA Tomb's Guards (7280) loses 0`; damaged unit `14789`; spoils ending `2531 silver [SILV]`.
- f95 t70, f73 t71, f73 t2: `battles` empty, and an existing assertion in each still passing — the
  point is that nothing else moved.

`packages/browser-core/src/parseReportFull.test.ts`:
- the two battles on the parsed fixture, by their camelCase names. The only test that can catch a
  serde naming mismatch.

## User-facing decisions

None. This bead stops at the boundary and shows nothing; the view is the sibling bead under the
parent ah-1is, which will need the navigator and a mockup.

Three judgements taken here so the implementation does not have to stop and ask:
- battles live on `ParsedReport`, not on `ReportHeader` and emphatically not on `ReportParseResult`;
- `parse_battles` is an independent pass over the preamble slice rather than a callee of
  `parse_header`;
- the statistics blocks stay as text, and the size question the bead raised is answered by the
  measurement above rather than escalated.

## Out of scope

- Any UI.
- Battles from merged allied reports — see the parent, ah-1is.
- Modelling round statistics field by field. If that is ever wanted it is its own bead, and the text
  is retained so nothing is lost in the meantime.
- Breaking a roster body down into items and skills. `unit.rs` is reused for what it already handles;
  a second unit parser is not written here.
- Linking a battle to the map hex. The coordinate is parsed so a later view can, but nothing here
  consumes it.
- Anything touching `ReportParseResult`, the persisted summary.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-core
cargo test --workspace
pnpm -r run test
pnpm run check
```

Manually, against `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-f95-t71.rep` (the battle section is lines
57-1473): two battles, the second `Sail (16352)` attacking `Looter (16779)` in `ocean (26,52)`.
Nothing to click.

Say in the PR where the battles were put and why — the bead asks for that explicitly, and the
reasoning is the persistence one above.

## Known traps

- **Blank lines do not exist by the time the parser sees them.** `unwrap_lines` drops them
  (`crates/core/src/report/unwrap.rs:85`), so blocks cannot be split on blank lines. Split on the
  headline: within the section, a line that ends in `!` opens a new battle. That rule also catches
  an assassination headline, whose wording this repository has no fixture for.
- **The headline wraps.** `… in ocean (25,55) in` / `  Atlantis Ocean!` is two physical lines, joined
  by `unwrap_lines` only if it decides the continuation would not have fitted
  (`unwrap.rs:93-98`). Increment 2 must assert the province, which is the half that lives on the
  second physical line — if the join does not happen, that is a fact to find out at increment 2, not
  at the fixture.
- **The section's end is a header, not a blank.** In f95 it is `Events during turn:` at line 1474.
  End on any of the preamble section headers `parse_header` already recognises; a parser that runs
  to the end of the preamble swallows the events, the skill reports, the attitudes and the unclaimed
  silver line.
- **`Damaged units:` sits between the two casualty lines.** `Total Casualties:` /
  `Pirates (14789) loses 15.` / `Damaged units: 14789.` / `AA Tomb's Guards (7280) loses 0.` — a
  parser that reads casualties until a non-casualty line stops early and loses the attacker's zero.
- **A nested struct needs its own `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`.** `ParsedReport` carries the
  attribute, but serde does not propagate it into nested types, so `line_start` would cross the
  boundary as `line_start` while the hand-written mirror says `lineStart` — and TypeScript cannot
  catch it, because the mirror is hand-written. The field simply reads `undefined`. Increment 7 is
  what proves it.
- **`ReportParseResult` is the persisted one.** Adding battles there would roughly double a stored
  turn. `ParsedReport` is recomputed from raw text and costs nothing on disk. Getting these two the
  wrong way round is the single most expensive mistake available in this bead.
- **A roster body can be enormous** — one line in the fixture is forty-odd repeats of
  `#a hero/dwarf`. Keep it as one string; do not split it into a vector of tokens, and do not write
  a test that asserts the whole body literally.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — another agent usually holds it in a worktree. Branch from
  `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria: The Battles during turn section parses into an ordered list of battles, each with participants, location (terrain, coordinate, province), attacker and defender rosters, rounds with their loss lines, total casualties, damaged unit ids, spoils, and the source line span; the f95 turn-71 fixture yields its two battles with the values named in Validation; reports without battles parse to an empty list and are otherwise unchanged; the battles reach the TypeScript side through both adapters

title: See the battles of the turn
description:
## Summary

See every battle the turn report describes: who fought whom and where, how each side was made
up, what the rounds did, who died and what was taken.

## Problem

Battles are the part of a turn a player most wants to re-read, and they are the one large
section of the report the app throws away. `parse_header` names `"Battles during turn"` only to
skip it (`crates/core/src/report/header.rs:151`), so every battle line falls on the floor
without a warning — which is the parser's tolerant contract working as intended, but it means
the only way to read a battle is to open the `.rep` file in a text editor and scroll.

The section is not small. In `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-f95-t71.rep` the battles
run from line 57 to roughly line 1930 — most of the file — and hold two battles, each with:

```
AA Tomb's Guards (7280) attacks Pirates (14789) in ocean (25,55) in
  Atlantis Ocean!

Attackers:      <roster: unit, faction, flags, men, items, skills>
Defenders:      <roster>
Round 1:        <tactics bonuses, spells cast, "breathes Fire, killing 15">
                <side> loses <n>.
Round 1 statistics:   <per-unit, per-weapon attack tallies>
Total Casualties:
Pirates (14789) loses 15.
Damaged units: 14789.
Spoils: 3 magic crossbows [MXBO], ... 2531 silver [SILV].
```

## Scope

Two children, in order:

1. Parse the battle blocks in the core and carry them across the boundary.
2. A view in the workspace that lists the turn's battles and shows one in full.

## Out of scope

- Battles from merged allied reports. `merge_report_into_sightings`
  (`crates/core/src/report/merge.rs:135`) merges regions and sightings only; headers are not
  merged at all, so an ally's battles would need a deduplication story of their own. Worth doing
  later, deliberately, rather than falling out of this work by accident.
- Any simulation, prediction or replay of combat. This is reading what happened.
- Battle history across turns; that belongs with ah-jg6.
acceptance_criteria: Every battle in the loaded turn report can be read in the app: the participants, where it happened, each side's roster, the rounds, the casualties and the spoils

title: See faction-level information: attitudes, allowances and unclaimed silver
description:
## Summary

Somewhere to see the faction as a whole: who we have declared what towards, how much of our
region and mage allowances is spent, and how much silver is sitting unclaimed.

## Problem

The report says all of this and the app shows none of it. Two blocks of the preamble are read
past today:

```
Faction Status:
Regions: 3 (10)
Quartermasters: 0 (0)
Mages: 6 (6)
Apprentices: 0 (15)
...
Declared Attitudes (default Unfriendly):
Hostile : Creatures (2), The Guardsmen (1), Dark League (28), ...
Neutral : Fon (8).
Friendly : The Gaggle (22), Kiiran (3), ...
Ally : Wistful Thinking (27), ...
```

`parse_header` names `"Faction Status"` only to skip it
(`crates/core/src/report/header.rs:151`) and never looks at attitudes at all — the only mention
of attitudes in the core is the DECLARE order grammar (`crates/core/src/orders/grammar.rs:68`),
which is the writing side, not the reading side.

Unclaimed silver *is* parsed (`crates/core/src/report/header.rs:48`) and does reach the
TypeScript side as `ReportHeaderInfo.unclaimedSilver`
(`packages/core-client/src/index.ts:401`), but nothing renders it; the same is true of
`factionTypes`. Both are referenced only by test fixtures.

So "am I at my region limit?", "can I train another apprentice?", "is this faction an ally?" and
"how much have I forgotten to CLAIM?" all mean going back to the report text.

## Scope

**Parsing** — `crates/core/src/report/header.rs`

- Read the `Faction Status:` block into structured counts of used-of-maximum. Keep it
  key-agnostic rather than hard-coding four fields: NewOrigins prints `Regions`, standard
  Atlantis prints `Tax Regions` and `Trade Regions`, and a ruleset may print others. An
  unrecognised line should be carried, not dropped.
- Read `Declared Attitudes (default <X>):` into the default attitude plus, per attitude level,
  the factions declared at it (name and id). Entries wrap across lines; `unwrap_lines` already
  joins continuations, so the parser should see one logical line per attitude — confirm that
  against the real fixture rather than assuming it.
- Both blocks fall inside the preamble slice `parse_header` is given (everything before the
  first region block, `crates/core/src/report/mod.rs:94`), so the preamble boundary needs no
  change.
- Stay tolerant, as the rest of the parser is: a report without either block parses fine and
  leaves the fields empty.

**Boundary**

- Extend `ReportHeader` / `ReportHeaderInfo` with the new data and carry it through the wasm and
  Tauri adapters. Both serialise `ParsedReport` straight through with
  `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` (`crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:648`,
  `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:458`), so the TypeScript mirror in
  `packages/core-client/src/index.ts:391` is the only hand-written part to keep in step.

**UI**

- A faction view showing: faction name, id and types; unclaimed silver; the status counts as
  used-of-maximum; and the declared attitudes grouped by level with the default stated.
- All five collapsible panels are hex- or unit-scoped; every faction-scoped surface today is a
  header chip with a popover under it (`MergedFactionsPanel`, `TurnMessagesPanel`). The header
  already renders `Faction <name>` with the merged-factions chip hanging off it
  (`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx`), so making that the trigger for an anchored
  panel — dismissed on Escape and on an outside press, as `TurnMessagesPanel` does — fits better
  than a sixth dock panel: this is read occasionally, not watched while planning. Confirm the
  shape with the navigator before building it.
- Where a faction in the attitude lists is one whose report has been merged in, say so. Do not
  invent links to factions the app knows nothing about.

## Out of scope

- Writing or editing `DECLARE` orders from the view — reading only, for now.
- How attitudes and allowances changed since last turn; that belongs with ah-jg6.
- Any faction-level statistic the report does not state (income totals, item tallies).

## Validation

- `cargo test -p atlantis-core` — unit tests for both blocks, plus the real-report fixtures
  `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-f95-t71.rep` (attitudes at every level, wrapped
  entries, `Regions: 0 (0)`) and `...-f73-t71.rep` (`Regions: 3 (10)`, `Apprentices: 0 (15)`).
- `pnpm test && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`
- Manual: import f95 turn 71 and check the view against the report text — 6038 unclaimed silver,
  6 of 6 mages, 15 of 15 apprentices, default Unfriendly, Fon (8) neutral.
acceptance_criteria: The Faction Status block (region/quartermaster/mage/apprentice allowances as used-of-maximum) and the Declared Attitudes block (default attitude plus the factions declared at each level) are parsed from the report and exposed to the TypeScript side; a faction view shows those alongside the faction name, id, types and unclaimed silver; a report lacking either block still parses and the view degrades rather than breaking; the real f95 and f73 turn-71 fixtures are covered by tests

title: Toggle to hide problems in the region panel
description:
## Problem

The `Problems` section sits at the top of the region panel body, above the region facts
(`packages/shared/src/workspace/RegionPanel.tsx:71`). When a hex carries several order
diagnostics the list grows and pushes population, tax base, wages, products and the rest of
the region info down out of view, so the user has to scroll past problems they have already
read to reach the numbers they came for.

## Scope

- Add a toggle that hides the Problems section in the region panel while leaving the rest of
  the panel in place.
- The toggle must stay visible when the section is hidden, and it should say how many problems
  are hidden, so the user can never lose track of unresolved diagnostics. The header `actions`
  slot on `CollapsiblePanel` is the natural place for it.
- When there are no problems for the hex the toggle should not appear at all — the section
  already renders nothing in that case.
- Persist the choice the same way panel collapse is persisted, in `workspaceStore`
  (`Persisted` picks `collapsed`/`layers`/`badges`; add the new flag to that set and to
  `reconcile`), so the preference survives a reload.

## Out of scope

- Any change to how diagnostics are computed, ordered or navigated.
- Toggles for other sections of the region panel, or for other panels.

## Validation

- `pnpm test` (unit tests for `RegionPanel` and `workspaceStore`)
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`
- Manual: select a hex with several diagnostics, hide problems, confirm the region facts move
  up to the top of the body; reload and confirm the choice stuck; select a clean hex and
  confirm no toggle is shown.
design:
## Context

`Problems` renders at the top of the region panel body, above everything the panel says about the
hex (`packages/shared/src/workspace/RegionPanel.tsx:71`). On a hex carrying several diagnostics the
list pushes population, tax base, wages, products, exits and structures down out of view, so
reaching the numbers means scrolling past problems already read.

When this lands: a chip in the region panel's header turns the section off, the facts come back to
the top of the body, and the chip keeps saying how many problems are put away.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`packages/shared/src/workspaceStore.ts`** — one persisted boolean.
  - `regionProblemsShown: boolean`, default `true`, with `toggleRegionProblems()` beside
    `togglePanel`/`toggleLayer`/`toggleBadge` (`:220-235`).
  - Add it to `Persisted` (`:172`), to `partialize` (`:247-251`) and to `merge` (`:262-268`).
  - **`reconcile` does not apply.** It reconciles a `Record<K, boolean>` against a known key set; a
    bare boolean needs its own guard —
    `typeof stored.regionProblemsShown === "boolean" ? stored.regionProblemsShown : true`. The
    reasoning in `reconcile`'s comment is the reason: a missing key must read as the default, not
    as `false`, or an upgrade silently hides the section for everyone who has ever saved a layout.
  - Add it to `resetWorkspaceStore` (`:283-285`), or tests leak the flag between cases.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/RegionPanel.tsx`** — the chip and the conditional section.
  - Pass `actions` to the `CollapsiblePanel` in the *hex* branch only (`:59-66`); the no-hex branch
    at `:39` has no problems to speak of.
  - Render the chip only when `problems.length > 0` — the section already renders nothing in that
    case, and a control for an empty section is furniture.
  - `<Problems problems={problems} />` at `:71` renders only while shown. Nothing else moves; the
    facts reach the top because the section above them is gone.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/LayerChips.tsx`** — the chip is copied from here (`:41-53`): a
  `<label>` wrapping a real `<input type="checkbox">`, lit `border-select bg-select/15 text-ink`
  when on and `border-edge text-ink-dim` when off. A real checkbox, not a styled `div`, so the
  smoke suite and a screen reader both address it by role and name. Give it
  `data-testid="region-problems-toggle"` and `aria-label="Problems"`; the count goes in the visible
  label beside it, as `LayerChips` puts its label text.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/CollapsiblePanel.tsx`** — unchanged. The `actions` slot already
  exists and already renders whether the panel is folded or open.

## Increments

1. **The preference.** RED: `workspaceStore.test.ts` — `the region panel shows its problems until
   told otherwise` and `toggling the problems section survives a reload`. GREEN: the flag, the
   action, `partialize`, `merge` and `resetWorkspaceStore`.
2. **The chip appears, and only when it should.** RED: `RegionPanel.test.tsx` (new) — no toggle on a
   hex with no problems, a toggle carrying the count on a hex with three. GREEN: the `actions` slot
   in the hex branch.
3. **It hides the section.** RED: the smoke case below. GREEN: the conditional around `Problems`.
   Read the trap about `renderToStaticMarkup` before writing this one — the hidden state cannot be
   proven in the unit test, and increment 3 is deliberately smoke-first for that reason.

## The test plan

Suites: `pnpm -r run test` (shared) and `pnpm run test:smoke`. `pnpm run check` before the PR.
Nothing here reaches `crates/`.

`packages/shared/src/workspaceStore.test.ts`:
- `the region panel shows its problems until told otherwise` — the default is `true`.
- `toggling the problems section is remembered` — `partialize` carries the flag.
- `a stored layout written before this flag existed still shows the problems` — `merge` with the key
  absent gives `true`. This is the upgrade case, and the one a `reconcile`-shaped fix gets wrong.
- `a stored value that is not a boolean is ignored` — `"yes"`, `0`, `null` each give `true`.

`packages/shared/src/workspace/RegionPanel.test.tsx` (new; follow `LayerChips.test.tsx`'s
`renderToStaticMarkup` + `beforeEach(resetWorkspaceStore)` shape):
- `offers no problems toggle on a hex with nothing wrong` — no `region-problems-toggle` in the
  markup.
- `puts a problems toggle in the header, with the count` — the toggle is there, reads `Problems`
  and `3`, and is a real checkbox.
- `shows the problems by default` — `region-problems` present.

`tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` (or `persistence.spec.ts`, whichever the implementer finds the
better home — the reload idiom is documented at `tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts:14`):
- `hiding the problems brings the region facts to the top` — select a hex with diagnostics, uncheck
  the chip, assert `region-problems` is gone, the chip is still there and still says 3, and the
  first thing in the panel body is the region's own line.
- `the hidden problems stay hidden across a reload` — `page.reload()`, same hex, still hidden.

## User-facing decisions

**Asked:** what the control looks like and what it says. The bead settles the behaviour — visible
while hidden, carrying a count, absent on a clean hex, persisted like panel collapse — so only the
appearance was open. Three candidates were drawn, each shown and hidden: a chip in the panel header,
a verb button (`Hide problems (3)` / `Show problems (3)`) in the same slot, and a caret folding the
section in place.

**Chosen by the navigator: 1, the chip in the panel header.** The map's layer strip is already this
application's word for "this is on, and turning it off hides something", so there is nothing new to
learn; the count rides on the control rather than disappearing with the section; and the section
header in the body keeps reading exactly as it does today.

Mockup: **`docs/ui/region-problems-toggle.html`**, merged on main by the navigator as PR #153. Read
it before starting; it is the record of the decision, and nothing in this bead re-opens it.

## Out of scope

- How diagnostics are computed, ordered or navigated.
- A toggle for any other section of the region panel, or for any other panel. If this one is liked,
  generalising it is a later bead with a wider question behind it.
- The orders panel's own diagnostics list, which is a different audience and stays as it is.
- Changing what `Problems` renders when it is shown.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm -r run test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check
```

Manually: select a hex with several diagnostics, uncheck the chip, and confirm the region facts sit
at the top of the body; reload and confirm the choice stuck; select a hex with nothing wrong and
confirm no chip appears at all.

## Known traps

- **`renderToStaticMarkup` cannot see a changed store.** Zustand serves its *initial* state to
  `useSyncExternalStore`'s server snapshot, so a store mutated before or during the render comes
  back unchanged — `LayerChips.test.tsx:31-35` says so in as many words, and only its
  "everything is on" case is provable there. So the *hidden* rendering belongs to the smoke suite,
  against a real store in a real browser. A unit test that appears to prove hiding is proving
  nothing, and will keep passing when the feature breaks.
- **`reconcile` is for records, not for a boolean.** Reaching for it because the neighbours use it
  produces either a type error or, worse, a coerced `false`. Write the two-line guard, and pin it
  with the "written before this flag existed" test.
- **A missing stored key must read as *shown*.** The store's own comment explains why a missing key
  defaulting to `false` is the dangerous direction: a mark quietly gone with nothing on screen to
  say why. Here it would hide every player's diagnostics on upgrade.
- **`resetWorkspaceStore` must learn the new flag**, or one test hides the section for every test
  that runs after it, and the failure lands somewhere unrelated.
- **The panel renders `CollapsiblePanel` twice.** The no-hex branch at `RegionPanel.tsx:39` is easy
  to miss and easy to wrongly give the chip to.
- **WebKit's driver returns `""` for text it considers clipped.** The header now carries a chip
  beside a title, a hint and the caret. Match the smoke assertions on `data-testid` and on the
  checkbox's accessible name rather than on the header's full text, or the native shell reports an
  empty string while Chromium passes.
- **Keep it a real `<input type="checkbox">`.** The lit/dim styling is the visible half; the input
  is what `getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Problems" })` and a screen reader need.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — another agent usually holds it in a worktree. Branch from
  `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria: A control in the region panel hides the Problems section and shows the region facts at the top of the panel body; the control remains visible with a count of the hidden problems; it is absent when the hex has no problems; the choice persists across a reload

title: A hex named only by a neighbour's exits is forgotten next turn
description:
## Summary

A hex known only from a neighbour's exits disappears from the map as soon as the unit that saw it
moves away. Load turn X and the unvisited neighbour A,B is drawn; load turn X+1 with the unit
elsewhere and A,B is gone, along with everything the report already told us about it.

The map forgets sighted-but-unvisited ground, so it shrinks back to the fringe of wherever the
faction currently stands rather than accumulating. That is the opposite of what the region-sightings
store exists to do.

## Problem

`buildHexMapModel` (`packages/shared/src/hexMapModel.ts:203`) assembles the map from three passes,
weakest knowledge first so stronger overwrites it:

1. `named` — hexes taken from `parsed.regions[].exits`, i.e. **the current report only**
   (`hexMapModel.ts:212-233`)
2. `stale` — hexes from the stored sightings of earlier turns (`hexMapModel.ts:235-254`)
3. `current` — hexes in this turn's report (`hexMapModel.ts:256-267`)

Pass 1 reads the current report and nothing else. Pass 2 reads stored sightings, and those only ever
cover visited regions: `region_sightings` in `crates/core/src/report/sighting.rs:40` maps
`report.regions` and nothing more, so an exit-only neighbour is never written as a sighting of its
own.

So a `named` hex lives exactly as long as the report that named it is the one on screen. Nothing
carries it into the next turn.

The persistence layer is not at fault and needs no change. `upsert_region_sightings`
(`crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs:1221`) is cumulative — it upserts on
`excluded.last_seen_turn >= region_sightings.last_seen_turn` and never deletes — so visited hexes
accumulate correctly. Only the exit-only ones were never offered to it.

## The fact is already stored

No schema change or migration is needed, and no data has been lost.

`RegionSighting.payload_json` is the whole `ReportRegion` serialized
(`sighting.rs:55`, pinned by `the_payload_is_the_whole_region`), and `ReportRegion` carries its
`exits` (`crates/core/src/report/model.rs:163`). `toStoredRegions`
(`packages/shared/src/gameMemory.ts:35`) passes that payload through as `StoredRegion.region`.

Every exit ever seen is therefore already sitting in the store, attached to the visited region that
named it. `buildHexMapModel` simply never walks `stored.region.exits` — only `parsed.regions[].exits`.

## Scope

- Pass 1 of `buildHexMapModel` should draw on the exits of stored regions as well as those of the
  current report, so a hex named in an earlier turn stays named.
- Decide what such a hex carries, and pin it with a test. Two questions the implementer must settle
  with the navigator rather than guess:
  - **`lastSeenTurn` and `ageInTurns`.** A `named` hex currently carries `null` for both
    (`hexMapModel.ts:225-226`). A hex named three turns ago is a weaker claim than one named this
    turn, and the fade and the stale cap are built on exactly that distinction.
  - **Precedence among competing exits.** Two stored regions from different turns can name the same
    hex with different terrain. The most recent naming is the obvious winner, but the current
    `if (byKey.has(key)) continue` keeps the *first* one encountered, which is arbitrary once
    stored regions join the loop.
- Keep the existing precedence intact: a visited hex must still beat a named one, and a current
  region must still beat a stored sighting.

## Out of scope

- Writing exit-only hexes as sightings of their own. The fact is already stored inside the visited
  region's payload; adding a second, weaker row for the same hex would need a migration and a rule
  for which row wins, to recover something already in hand.
- How an unsurveyed hex is drawn. `ah-rgp` settled the wash and the unsurveyed rim; this bead is
  about *whether the hex is on the map at all*, not what it looks like once it is.
- Map export (`mapExport.ts`), beyond whatever falls out of the model change.

## Validation

- A unit test in `hexMapModel.test.ts`, alongside the two that already cover named hexes
  (`marks a neighbour named only by an exit as known by name`, `lets a stored sighting override a
  hex merely named by an exit`): build a model from a turn X+1 report that does not name A,B, with a
  stored region from turn X whose exits do, and assert A,B is present and `named`.
- Manually with two consecutive real reports: load turn X, note an unvisited neighbour at the fringe,
  load turn X+1 with the unit moved away, and confirm the hex is still drawn.
- `pnpm run test` and the smoke suite stay green; the existing precedence tests must not need
  editing.
acceptance_criteria: A hex named by the exits of a region seen in an earlier turn is still drawn as a named hex after the unit that saw it has moved away and the next turn is loaded; a visited hex still beats a named one and a current region still beats a stored sighting; covered by a test in hexMapModel.test.ts
close_reason: Delivered in PR #149 (squash a8ba263): named hexes now come from remembered regions' exits as well as the report on screen

title: One gate at a time, machine-wide
description:
playwright.config.ts records its own measurement: one worker already drives this machine to about 280% CPU, and two workers broke both interactivity guards, because a test that measures how long the main thread is blocked measures contention instead.

N agents each running pnpm check reproduces exactly that, off-config. With retries: 1 the likely outcome is a flaky red that an agent then classifies as infrastructure and re-runs for free under its own rules - so either the loop burns wall-clock, or a retry-green means an agent merged on a measurement it never actually satisfied.

The gate takes an exclusive machine-wide lock so agents queue instead of contending. The same lock incidentally serialises cargo on the shared build directory.
acceptance_criteria:
pnpm check (at minimum test:smoke and test:pwa) acquires an exclusive lock before running and releases it afterwards, including on failure.
A crashed holder cannot deadlock the others.
Two agents running the gate at once produce two sequential runs, both honest.

title: Roads do not shrink with the map when zooming out
description:
## Summary

Zoomed far out, roads stop being lines and become blobs: the mark is wider than the hex it belongs
to. Reported against Miniature World and Beveled Tile, but the cause is shared and **every theme has
it** — they differ only in degree.

Each theme's `RoadLayer` draws a spoke from the hex centre along `ROAD_VECTORS[direction]`, scaled by
`HEX_RADIUS * 0.87` (0.83 in Beveled Tile). The **length** is therefore hex-relative and shrinks with
the world transform. The **width** is not: every road line carries
`vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke"`, which pins the stroke to a constant number of screen pixels at
any zoom. Nothing in any theme divides a road width by the scale or expresses it in fractions of
`HEX_RADIUS`, and the CSS road classes set colour only, never width — the JSX `strokeWidth` is the
whole story.

At `MIN_STEP = -8` the scale is 0.25 (`mapViewport.ts:35-37,78-80`), so an 18-unit hex is 4.5px on
screen and a spoke is about 3.9px long:

| theme | road stroke (constant screen px) | spoke at min zoom | width ÷ length |
|---|---|---|---|
| classic | 7 | 3.9px | ~1.8× |
| miniatureWorld | 5 | 3.9px | ~1.3× |
| beveledTile | 4 | 3.7px | ~1.1× |
| cartographersTable | 4 casing + 1.4 dash | 3.9px | ~1.0× |
| emblemAndDots | 3.4 | 3.9px | ~0.87× |
| tacticalHud | 2 | 3.9px | ~0.51× |

It reads worst at far zoom because the zoom-band CSS deliberately hides labels, pips, chips and
glyphs there while **keeping** roads (each theme.css says so — e.g. beveledTile "far keeps the tile,
its bevel and the roads"). So the fattest thing on screen is the only thing left on screen.

## Scope

- The six `RoadLayer` functions: `classic/index.tsx:58`, `cartographersTable/index.tsx:168`,
  `beveledTile/index.tsx:179`, `emblemAndDots/index.tsx:137`, `tacticalHud/index.tsx:159`,
  `miniatureWorld/index.tsx:216`.
- Agreed target: **a road keeps its proportion to the hex at every zoom.** In this codebase that
  means dropping `vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke"` from the road marks and expressing the width in
  fractions of `HEX_RADIUS`, which is the rule `mapThemes/geometry.ts:4-6` already states for marks:
  "in fractions of HEX_RADIUS rather than in absolute pixels". Each theme keeps its own relative
  weight — Tactical HUD's road stays the thinnest, Miniature World's the heaviest.
- Regression test modelled on the one that already pins the opposite behaviour for the fog lattice,
  `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:2011` ("the unexplored lattice keeps a constant hairline at every
  zoom"). That test asserts computed `stroke-width × --map-scale === 1` screen pixel. A road wants
  the mirror of it: computed `stroke-width` constant in **user** units across zoom steps, so its
  screen width falls with the scale. Assert it at rest, zoomed in, and at `MIN_STEP`.
- No theme currently has any test asserting a road's width or its scaling — the road tests only
  count lines and check for dashes. Whatever shape the fix takes, that gap is what let this ship.

## Two things the fix has to decide, not assume

1. **Does a road still read at far zoom once it shrinks?** The far band keeps roads precisely
   because they are the last legible structure. A width that is a true fraction of the hex is about
   1px on screen at `MIN_STEP`. If that turns out to be too faint, the honest answer is a floor
   expressed against the hex (never wider than some share of it) rather than a return to a constant
   screen width. Look at it before choosing.
2. **The route overlay is also non-scaling** (`MapCanvas.tsx:736,744` — a 5px casing and a 3px line),
   and Classic's road width of 7 was tuned explicitly against it, per the comment at
   `classic/index.tsx:52-57`: wide enough that "whether a path runs along a road or misses it stays
   legible at every zoom". If roads scale and the route overlay does not, that relationship inverts
   somewhere in the zoom range. Decide whether the overlay follows the roads.

## Out of scope

- Labels, pips, chips and the fog hairline, which are constant-screen-size deliberately and have
  their own zoom-band rules.
- Any change to road *placement* or to which hexes report roads.
- Classic, if `ah-xde` (removing that theme) has landed first — it is the worst offender at 7px, so
  the order of these two beads decides whether it is worth touching.

## Validation

- `pnpm test` — the theme road tests, plus whatever unit-level assertion the fix adds.
- `pnpm test:smoke` — both shells, including the new road-scaling test.
- `pnpm check` before the PR.
- By hand, and this is the part that actually answers it: open a hex with roads in Miniature World
  and Beveled Tile, zoom to `MIN_STEP`, and confirm a road reads as a line within its hex rather
  than a blob across it — then zoom to `MAX_STEP` and confirm it has not become a slab.
design: Target agreed with the navigator: a road keeps its proportion to the hex at every zoom. The cause is vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke" on every road line, which pins the width to screen pixels while the spoke length stays hex-relative - so the two diverge as the map scales. Reported for Miniature World and Beveled Tile; investigation found all six themes affected, Classic worst at 7px against a 3.9px spoke at minimum zoom. Two questions are left open on purpose because they need to be looked at rather than reasoned about: whether a proportional road still reads at far zoom, where the zoom band keeps roads as the last visible structure, and whether the route overlay - also non-scaling, and what Classic's width was tuned against - should follow the roads.
acceptance_criteria:
At MIN_STEP a road reads as a line inside its hex rather than a mark wider than the hex, in every theme that ships.
A road's width is expressed against HEX_RADIUS rather than in constant screen pixels, so its on-screen width falls with the map scale.
A smoke test pins the scaling across zoom steps, mirroring the fog lattice's constant-hairline test rather than repeating it.
Each theme keeps its own relative road weight - the thin ones stay thin, the heavy ones stay heavy.
pnpm check passes.
notes:
Far-zoom question answered by looking, not reasoning: screenshots of all five themes at the fixture's road hex (1:7,53 and the mountain at 1:7,51), at step -4 and at MIN_STEP.

At -4 (the far band) every theme's road reads cleanly as a line inside its hex - the bug is gone and nothing was lost. At MIN_STEP (scale 0.25) Miniature World (1.25px), Beveled Tile and Cartographer's casing (1.0px) are still visible; Emblem and Dots (0.85px) is faint; Tactical HUD (0.5px) and Cartographer's dash (0.35px) are close to invisible. No road disappears outright across the band, so NO FLOOR was added, per the agreed rule. The fallback if it proves too faint in use is max(width, 1px / var(--map-scale)) in a style declaration - noted in tacticalHud/index.tsx beside its constant.

Second open question, decided with the navigator: the route overlay follows the roads (casing 5, line 3, risk outline 2, all now in hex units). The selection and focus rings on the same hexagon stay screen-constant, being chrome rather than ground.

Side effect worth watching in use: dash patterns were measured in the non-scaling space before and are hex-relative now, so at MIN_STEP the dotted route is ~1.5px on/off - the solid-vs-dotted distinction is still there but subtle.
close_reason: Delivered in PR #144. Roads in all five themes and the route overlay (casing, line, risk outline) now take their width from radii() instead of vectorEffect='non-scaling-stroke', so they shrink with the hex. Far-zoom question answered by screenshot, no floor needed; see the bead notes.

title: Remove the Classic map theme
description:
## Summary

Remove the **Classic** map theme. It is the map as it looked before the five designed themes
arrived, and it is now the least of them; keeping it costs a directory of drawing code, a share of
every theme-wide change, and a slot in the settings picker.

Classic is not an ordinary registry entry, which is what makes this more than a deletion. It is
**`DEFAULT_MAP_THEME_ID`**, and it is the hard-coded last resort inside `getMapTheme` for a registry
that contains no default at all. Both have to move before the directory can go.

**Cartographer's Table becomes the new default** (decided with the navigator).

## Scope

- Delete `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/classic/` — `index.tsx` and `classic.test.tsx`.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/index.ts`: drop the import and the `MAP_THEMES` entry,
  point `DEFAULT_MAP_THEME_ID` at `cartographers-table`, and replace the `?? classic` last resort in
  `getMapTheme` with the new default's module. Update the file header comment, which currently
  describes the order as "the map as it was, then the five designs".
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/index.test.tsx` — the registry tests name Classic
  directly, including the fallback-of-last-resort case.
- Persisted settings need no migration code: `knownMapTheme` in
  `packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts:142` already answers `DEFAULT_MAP_THEME_ID` for any id the
  registry does not know, so a stored `"classic"` moves to the new default on the next load. This is
  worth an explicit test rather than an assumption — a stored `"classic"` must land on
  Cartographer's Table, not throw and not render nothing.
- `tests/smoke/settings.spec.ts` — five assertions name `classic` or `map-theme-classic`, including
  the picker's default value and a test that switches away from Classic and back to it. They need
  rewriting around two themes that still ship.
- Docs, rewritten against the new default rather than merely struck: `docs/ui/hex-rendering.md`
  describes what is drawn largely in terms of what Classic draws (its opening note, the "not yet
  implemented" list at the foot); `docs/ui/README.md` says "All six ship: Classic, plus the five
  designs" and carries a Classic Commander layout section; `docs/ui/map-themes.md` is the registry's
  own reference.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/hexView.ts:53` mentions "the classic hull names" — that
  is Atlantis ship vocabulary, not the theme. Leave it.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the other five themes' drawing.
- A migration dialog or a notice telling the user their theme changed. The silent fallback is the
  agreed behaviour.

## Validation

- `pnpm test` — registry tests, the new stored-`"classic"` fallback test, settings store tests.
- `pnpm test:smoke` — both shells; the map theme picker walk is the one that moves most.
- `pnpm check` before the PR.
- By hand: open the app with `"classic"` already in `atlantis-hud-settings`, confirm the map draws
  as Cartographer's Table and the picker shows it, and confirm the picker no longer offers Classic.
design: Cartographer's Table becomes the new default, chosen with the navigator as the most map-like of the remaining five and the next in registry order. No migration code is written: knownMapTheme already answers DEFAULT_MAP_THEME_ID for an unknown id, so a stored "classic" moves across on the next load - the point is to test that rather than assume it. Docs are rewritten in the same bead rather than split off, because hex-rendering.md describes the map in terms of what Classic draws and would otherwise document a theme that no longer exists.
acceptance_criteria:
The settings picker no longer offers Classic, and packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/classic/ is gone.
DEFAULT_MAP_THEME_ID is cartographers-table, and getMapTheme's last resort for a registry without a default no longer mentions Classic.
A settings blob holding mapTheme "classic" loads as Cartographer's Table rather than failing or drawing nothing, pinned by a test.
docs/ui/hex-rendering.md, docs/ui/README.md and docs/ui/map-themes.md describe the themes that actually ship, with the rendering prose rewritten against the new default.
pnpm check passes.

title: Refresh the beads issues export at pre-push instead of on every commit
description:
`.beads/issues.jsonl` is a generated file that is committed so the backlog is diffable in the repo.
Keeping it fresh is currently an obligation on every commit: `export.auto: true` in
`.beads/config.yaml` makes the bd pre-commit hook write it, and the beads-workflow skill's
end-of-session checklist asks for `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl` by hand. Auto-export is
throttled to once a minute, and it has already committed a snapshot that still held a bead deleted
minutes earlier (#132 documented the trap and the `git show HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl | wc -l` check
that catches it). Two sessions in a row have then ended with the export knowingly out of date,
because refreshing it means a commit straight to `main`.

Move the obligation to push time, where it is needed once per branch instead of once per commit and
where nothing can be pushed stale.

## Scope

- A repo-owned gate that runs from `.beads/hooks/pre-push`, below the `BEADS INTEGRATION` markers
  so `bd hooks install` preserves it (`bd hooks install --help`: user content outside the markers
  survives installs and upgrades).
- The gate exports the database to a temporary file and compares it with the committed
  `.beads/issues.jsonl`. Equal: the push proceeds and the gate says nothing. Different: the gate
  writes the fresh export, commits that one file as `chore(beads): refresh the issues export`, and
  aborts the push with a message saying the commit was made and to push again.
- A pre-push hook cannot amend or extend the commits being pushed — the refs are already computed —
  so the refresh is a new commit and the push is aborted rather than rewritten. No `--force` is
  ever needed.
- `export.auto` goes to `false`, which is beads' own default, so no throttled snapshot can reach a
  commit again.
- The gate is inert when it cannot do its job: no `bd` on PATH, no `.beads` directory, or a
  `bd export` that fails must let the push through rather than block it. A tooling convenience must
  not stand between the player and their remote.
- The beads-workflow skill loses the per-session export step and gains a short description of the
  gate, replacing the trap section's manual verification advice.
- Repo tooling has no test home today, so the gate's decision logic is written to be unit-testable
  and a root vitest project is wired up for `scripts/`, run by `pnpm run check` and by the CI
  `checks` job.

## Out of scope

- Whether the export is committed at all — that question was settled in favour of keeping it.
- The Dolt remote and `bd dolt push`, which stay exactly as they are.
- The other four bd hooks.
- Any CI check that validates the export server-side.

## Validation

- Unit tests for the gate: unchanged export, changed export, missing `.beads`, absent `bd`, and a
  failing `bd export`.
- An end-to-end shell exercise in a throwaway git repo with a bare remote and a stubbed `bd` on
  PATH: a stale export aborts the first push with the refresh commit in place, and the second push
  succeeds with the fresh file in it.
- `pnpm run check` and the CI gate.
- Manually, on this branch: with a deliberately stale JSONL, `git push` refuses once, leaves the
  refresh commit, and succeeds on the retry.
acceptance_criteria:
A repo-owned gate runs from .beads/hooks/pre-push, below the beads markers, and survives bd hooks install.
A push whose committed .beads/issues.jsonl matches a fresh bd export proceeds silently.
A push whose committed export is stale is aborted, with the fresh export committed alone as chore(beads): refresh the issues export, and the retry succeeds.
No push is ever rewritten or needs --force.
export.auto is false in .beads/config.yaml.
The gate lets the push through when bd is absent, .beads is missing, or bd export fails.
The beads-workflow skill drops the per-session export step and describes the gate instead.
The gate's logic is covered by unit tests that run in pnpm run check and in CI.

title: Remember map zoom level and focus hex across reloads
description:
The map view resets when a game is reloaded. The user has to zoom and pan back to where they were working.

Goal: persist the map viewport per game so reloading restores the previous view.

Scope:
- Persist current zoom level and the focused/centered hex
- Restore them when the same game is loaded again
- Fall back to the current default view when no saved state exists (e.g. first load of a game)

Acceptance criteria:
- Reloading a game restores the zoom level and centered hex from the previous session
- Viewport state is stored per game, so switching between games does not mix up views

title: Map forgets known-but-never-occupied hexes once no unit can see them
description:
When a unit moves away, the map stops showing hexes that were known only from that unit's line of sight. Only the hex the unit itself occupied earlier remains on the map; the surrounding 6 hexes (e.g. ocean hexes seen from a fleet jump but never entered) disappear.

Expected: once a hex has been observed in any report, it stays on the map as known terrain (with the data from the last turn it was observed), even when no unit can currently see it.

Actual: only hexes a unit actually occupied are remembered; adjacent observed-only hexes are dropped when they leave current visibility.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hexes observed from an adjacent unit remain visible on the map after the unit leaves
- Remembered hexes show the terrain and data from the most recent turn they were observed
- Currently visible vs remembered hexes remain distinguishable (see ah-rgp)
close_reason: Duplicate of ah-ctf, delivered in PR #149 (squash a8ba263). All three acceptance criteria met: namings now come from remembered regions' exits, the most recent naming wins, and named hexes keep the ah-rgp unsurveyed rim. No work was ever committed under this bead - its branch held zero commits.

title: Option to keep the long order format when exporting orders
description:
Exported orders come out in the short format only. The server's own unit description — name,
flags, weight, capacity, skills and what the unit can study, wrapped over as many `;` lines as it
takes — is dropped the moment a report's template becomes an editable document
(`stripUnitComments` in `packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts`, called once from
`documentFor` in `packages/shared/src/orderDraft.ts:113`), and `exportOrders`
(`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx:1526`) writes that stripped document straight out.

Dropping the descriptions from the editor was deliberate (#37): the unit panel already says all of
it, and on a unit with no orders yet the description is the whole block. But the exported file is
read elsewhere — kept as a record of the turn, diffed against the next one, or read by a human
without this application in front of them — and there the long format is what makes a bare
`unit 793` legible:

```
unit 793
```

So the option belongs on the export, not on the editor: the descriptions stay out of the panel the
player writes in, and go back into the file on the way out when asked for.

## Scope

- An option on the orders export that puts the server's long-format unit descriptions back into the
  exported text. Default off, so today's output is unchanged unless the player asks.
- The descriptions are recovered from the report's own template (`parsed.ordersTemplate`), matched
  per `unit` block, rather than kept in the document — the document must stay as it is, or the
  editor regains the clutter #37 removed.
- Each unit's description is written directly under its `unit` line, above the player's orders, in
